1.m: Now therefore we shall explain the measuring cord. \1\

1.s: rajjuṃ pāśavatīṃ samāṃ nirāyatāṃ pṛṣṭhyāṃ yathārthamupakalpayet ||
1.d: रज्जुं पाशवतीं समां निरायतां पृष्ठ्यां यथार्थमुपकल्पयेत् ॥
1.m: One should prepare a straight, stretched cord provided with loops, for the axial line according to the purpose. \2\

1.s: antareṇa citrāsvātī śravaṇapratiśravaṇau kṛttikāpratikṛttike tiṣyapunarvasū ca prāgdeśo 'yaṃ yugamātroditayoḥ pāśāñca ||
1.d: अन्तरेण चित्रास्वाती श्रवणप्रतिश्रवणौ कृत्तिकाप्रतिकृत्तिके तिष्यपुनर्वसू च प्राग्देशो ऽयं युगमात्रोदितयोः पाशाञ्च ॥
1.m: Between Citrā and Svātī, Śravaṇa and Pratiśravaṇa, Kṛttikā and Pratikṛttikā, and Tiṣya and Punarvasu, when they have risen by the measure of a yoke, is the eastern direction; and [one prepares] the loops. \3\

1.s: dārśikyāḥ śayāḥ ṣaṭtāni sapta saptadaśaiva tu ekaṃ dve pañca tairmītvā samaraiḥ parilekhayet ||
1.d: दार्शिक्याः शयाः षट्तानि सप्त सप्तदशैव तु एकं द्वे पञ्च तैर्मीत्वा समरैः परिलेखयेत् ॥
1.m:
The cords of the New-Moon sacrifice are six; these are seven and seventeen indeed;

Having measured one, two, [and] five with them, one should trace around with equal cords. \4\

1.s: aṃsācchroṇau rajjvantaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya prācīmanulikhedaṃsepratiṣṭhāpya pratīcīṃ samare rajjvantaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya śroṇeradhyaṃsādanulikhet ||
1.d: अंसाच्छ्रोणौ रज्ज्वन्तं प्रतिष्ठाप्य प्राचीमनुलिखेदंसेप्रतिष्ठाप्य प्रतीचीं समरे रज्ज्वन्तं प्रतिष्ठाप्य श्रोणेरध्यंसादनुलिखेत् ॥
1.m: Fixing the end of the cord from the shoulder to the buttock, one should trace eastward; fixing [it] at the shoulder, [one should trace] westward; fixing the end of the cord on the equal cord, one should trace from above the buttock to the shoulder. \5\
In the same way to the north, in front, and behind. \6\

1.s: aratniścaturaśrastu pūrvasyāgneḥ kharo bhavet rathacakrākṛtiḥ paścāccandrārdhena tu dakṣiṇe ||
1.d: अरत्निश्चतुरश्रस्तु पूर्वस्याग्नेः खरो भवेत् रथचक्राकृतिः पश्चाच्चन्द्रार्धेन तु दक्षिणे ॥
1.m:
A square of one cubit shall be the mound of the eastern fire;

In the shape of a chariot-wheel in the west, and in the form of a half-moon in the south. \7\

1.s: madhyāt koṭipramāṇena maṇḍalaṃ parilekhayet atiriktatribhāgena sarvaṃ tu sahamaṇḍalam caturaśre 'kṣṇayā rajjurmadhyataḥ saṃnipātayet parilekhya tadardhenārdhamaṇḍalameva tat ||
1.d: मध्यात् कोटिप्रमाणेन मण्डलं परिलेखयेत् अतिरिक्तत्रिभागेन सर्वं तु सहमण्डलम् चतुरश्रे ऽक्ष्णया रज्जुर्मध्यतः संनिपातयेत् परिलेख्य तदर्धेनार्धमण्डलमेव तत् ॥

1.s: gārhapatyāhavanīyāvantarā rajjuṃ nimāyāparasmiṃstṛtīye lakṣaṇam | madhyāt turīyamutsṛjya lakṣaṇaṃ pāśāntau samāhṛtya dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇāgnerlakṣaṇam ||
1.d: गार्हपत्याहवनीयावन्तरा रज्जुं निमायापरस्मिंस्तृतीये लक्षणम् । मध्यात् तुरीयमुत्सृज्य लक्षणं पाशान्तौ समाहृत्य दक्षिणतो दक्षिणाग्नेर्लक्षणम् ॥
1.m: Having measured the cord between the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires, [one makes] a mark at the western third; having cast off a fourth from the center, [and] having brought the two loop-ends together, the mark for the Dakṣiṇāgni fire is to the south. \9\
Reversing this very [procedure], the mark of the rubbish heap is to the north. \10\

1.s: yāvatpramāṇā rajjuḥ syāttāvadevāgamo bhavet āgamārdhe bhavecchaṅkuḥ śaṅkorardhe nirāñchanam ||
1.d: यावत्प्रमाणा रज्जुः स्यात्तावदेवागमो भवेत् आगमार्धे भवेच्छङ्कुः शङ्कोरर्धे निराञ्छनम् ॥
1.m:
As great as the measure of the cord may be, so great shall be the extension;

At half of the extension shall be a peg; at half of the peg [distance] shall be an intermediate mark. \11\
This rule is proclaimed for equilateral squares. \12\ \1\

2.s: aṣṭāśītiḥ śatamīṣā tiryagakṣaścatuḥśatam ṣaḍaśītiryugaṃ cāsya rathaścārakya ucyate ||
2.d: अष्टाशीतिः शतमीषा तिर्यगक्षश्चतुःशतम् षडशीतिर्युगं चास्य रथश्चारक्य उच्यते ॥
2.m:
The pole is one hundred and eighty-eight; the transverse axle is one hundred and four;

And its yoke is eighty-six: this is called the Cāraka cart. \1\

2.s: īṣāyāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ mītvā ṣaṭsu navasu ca lakṣaṇe tricatvāriṃśake pāśo 'ṅgulānāṃ niyogataḥ ||
2.d: ईषायां लक्षणं मीत्वा षट्सु नवसु च लक्षणे त्रिचत्वारिंशके पाशो ऽङ्गुलानां नियोगतः ॥
2.m:
Having measured a mark on the pole, there are marks at six and at nine;

At forty-three is the loop, by the placement of finger-breadths. \2\

2.s: eṣā vediḥ samākhyātā cārakya rathasaṃmitā aindrāgnasya paśoreṣā paśuṣvanyeṣu ṣaṭśayā ||
2.d: एषा वेदिः समाख्याता चारक्य रथसंमिता ऐन्द्राग्नस्य पशोरेषा पशुष्वन्येषु षट्शया ॥
2.m:
This altar is declared to be measured by the Cāraka cart;

This is for the animal sacrifice to Indra and Agni; in the case of other animal sacrifices it has six cords. \3\

2.s: prācyardhaḥ ṣaḍaratniḥ syādardhāratnernirāñchanam ardhe śroṇī tato 'rdheṃ 'sāvadhyardha iti pāśukī ||
2.d: प्राच्यर्धः षडरत्निः स्यादर्धारत्नेर्निराञ्छनम् अर्धे श्रोणी ततो ऽर्धें ऽसावध्यर्ध इति पाशुकी ॥
2.m:
The eastern half shall be six cubits; at half a cubit is the intermediate mark;

At half [that distance] are the two buttocks; then at half [that distance] are the two shoulders, [and] at one and a half: such is [the altar] for animal sacrifices. \4\

2.s: paśādardhaśaye śroṇī dvayoḥ pṛṣṭhyāparā dvayoḥ prācyardhastu tato 'dhyardhe tato 'dhyardhe nirāñchanam ardheṃ 'so 'dhyardha evānyastato 'dhyardheṃ 'sa uttaraḥ aratnau tu tataḥ pāśo vedī mārutī vārūṇī ||
2.d: पशादर्धशये श्रोणी द्वयोः पृष्ठ्यापरा द्वयोः प्राच्यर्धस्तु ततो ऽध्यर्धे ततो ऽध्यर्धे निराञ्छनम् अर्धें ऽसो ऽध्यर्ध एवान्यस्ततो ऽध्यर्धें ऽस उत्तरः अरत्नौ तु ततः पाशो वेदी मारुती वारूणी ॥

2.s: sarvā daśaśayā rajjurmadhye cāsyā nirāñchanam prācyardhaṃ pañcame kuryāddikkuṣṭhā paitṛkī smṛtā ||
2.d: सर्वा दशशया रज्जुर्मध्ये चास्या निराञ्छनम् प्राच्यर्धं पञ्चमे कुर्याद्दिक्कुष्ठा पैतृकी स्मृता ॥
2.m:
The entire cord has ten spans, and in its center is an intermediate mark;

One should make the eastern half at the fifth; the [altar] oriented to the quarters is traditional for the ancestors. \6\

2.s: sarvā saptaśayā rajjurmadhye cāsyā nirāñchanam prācyardhaṃ pañcame kuryāddikkuṣṭhā paitṛkī smṛtā ||
2.d: सर्वा सप्तशया रज्जुर्मध्ये चास्या निराञ्छनम् प्राच्यर्धं पञ्चमे कुर्याद्दिक्कुष्ठा पैतृकी स्मृता ॥
2.m:
The entire cord has seven spans, and in its center is an intermediate mark;

One should make the eastern half at the fifth; the [altar] oriented to the quarters is traditional for the ancestors. \7\ \2\

3.s: prāgvaṃśaṃ daśakaṃ kuryātpatnīśālāṃ catuḥśayām prāgvaṃśāttriṣu vedyanto vedyantāt prakrame sadaḥ ||
3.d: प्राग्वंशं दशकं कुर्यात्पत्नीशालां चतुःशयाम् प्राग्वंशात्त्रिषु वेद्यन्तो वेद्यन्तात् प्रक्रमे सदः ॥
3.m:
One should make the hall facing east of ten [measures]; the hall for the patron's wife of four cords;

From the hall facing east the end of the altar is at three; from the end of the altar the sadas shed is at a stride. \1\

3.s: navakaṃ tu sado vidyāccatvāraḥ sadaso 'ntaram catvārastrikā havirdhānamardhadaśāstadantaram ||
3.d: नवकं तु सदो विद्याच्चत्वारः सदसो ऽन्तरम् चत्वारस्त्रिका हविर्धानमर्धदशास्तदन्तरम् ॥
3.m:
One should know the sadas shed to be of nine; four [measures] is the interval of the sadas shed;

Four triads is the Havirdhāna shed; nine and a half is their interval. \2\

3.s: padaṃ yūpāvaṭe mītvā śeṣamauttaravedikam āgnīdhraṃ ṣaḍaratnyeva ṣaṭtriṃśatprakramā rajjuḥ ||
3.d: पदं यूपावटे मीत्वा शेषमौत्तरवेदिकम् आग्नीध्रं षडरत्न्येव षट्त्रिंशत्प्रक्रमा रज्जुः ॥
3.m:
Having measured a foot for the sacrificial post-hole, the remainder belongs to the high altar;

The Āgnīdhra shed is just six cubits; thirty-six strides is the cord. \3\

3.s: lakṣikā dvādaśa trikā | vedisadohavirdhānāni minotyevānupūrvaśaḥ pañcadaśakamekaviṃśakaṃ trikamaparam | parato 'parastriko dvādaśasu ca pāśada ucyate | some rajju nimānamuttamam ||
3.d: लक्षिका द्वादश त्रिका । वेदिसदोहविर्धानानि मिनोत्येवानुपूर्वशः पञ्चदशकमेकविंशकं त्रिकमपरम् । परतो ऽपरस्त्रिको द्वादशसु च पाशद उच्यते । सोमे रज्जु निमानमुत्तमम् ॥
3.m: Twelve triad-marks; he measures the altar, sadas shed, and Havirdhāna shed in succession: a fifteen, a twenty-one, another triad; beyond is another triad, and at twelve is called the loop-giver; this is the supreme measurement of the cord in the Soma sacrifice. \4\

3.s: tripadā pārśvamānī syāttiryaṅmānī padaṃ bhavet tasyākṣṇayā tu yā rajjuḥ kuryāddaśapadāṃ tayā ||
3.d: त्रिपदा पार्श्वमानी स्यात्तिर्यङ्मानी पदं भवेत् तस्याक्ष्णया तु या रज्जुः कुर्याद्दशपदां तया ॥
3.m:
The flank measure shall be three feet; the transverse measure shall be a foot;

With the cord which is its diagonal, one should make [an area] of ten feet. \5\

3.s: paśādardhacaturdaśe navake tu tataḥ punaḥ ardhacaturdaśaḥ pāśaḥ sadasaśchedanamuttamam ||
3.d: पशादर्धचतुर्दशे नवके तु ततः पुनः अर्धचतुर्दशः पाशः सदसश्छेदनमुत्तमम् ॥
3.m:
At the loop, at thirteen and a half, then again at nine;

Thirteen and a half is the loop: this is the supreme cutting-out of the sadas shed. \6\
Having measured the cord by ten chariot-axles and eleven of the measure of an upper pestle-base, they declare a twenty-fourth part of it to be the individual altar for the Ekādaśinī. \7\

3.s: śikhaṇḍinī cetkartavyā vedyantāddvyardhamuddharet aṣṭāṅgulaṃ tadardhaṃ syāddevya vedi prasiddhaye taṃ prāñcaṃ tu samīkṣeta tāṃstu vidyācchikhaṇḍinīm ||
3.d: शिखण्डिनी चेत्कर्तव्या वेद्यन्ताद्द्व्यर्धमुद्धरेत् अष्टाङ्गुलं तदर्धं स्याद्देव्य वेदि प्रसिद्धये तं प्राञ्चं तु समीक्षेत तांस्तु विद्याच्छिखण्डिनीम् ॥

3.s: pañcakaṃ saptaṃ caiva ekamekaṃ tataḥ punaḥ eṣā vediḥ samākhyātā kaukilyāstvatha cārake ||
3.d: पञ्चकं सप्तं चैव एकमेकं ततः पुनः एषा वेदिः समाख्याता कौकिल्यास्त्वथ चारके ॥
3.m:
Five and seven, and then one each again;

This altar is declared for the Kaukili [Sautrāmaṇī] in the Cāraka school. \9\ \3\

4.s: janmanā rogahīno vā yajamāno bhavedyadi kathaṃ tatra pramāṇāni prayoktavyāni kartṛbhiḥ ||
4.d: जन्मना रोगहीनो वा यजमानो भवेद्यदि कथं तत्र प्रमाणानि प्रयोक्तव्यानि कर्तृभिः ॥
4.m:
If the sacrificer should be free of illness from birth,

How should the measures be applied there by the builders? \1\

4.s: tuṇḍaṃ puṣkaranālasya ṣaḍguṇaṃ pariveṣṭitam trihāyaṇyā vatsataryā vālena samamiṣyate ||
4.d: तुण्डं पुष्करनालस्य षड्गुणं परिवेष्टितम् त्रिहायण्या वत्सतर्या वालेन सममिष्यते ॥
4.m:
The tip of a lotus-stalk wound around six times

Is held to be equal to a hair of a three-year-old heifer. \2\

4.s: trayastrihāyaṇīvālāḥ sarṣapārdhaṃ vidhīyate dviguṇaṃ sarṣapaṃ prāhuryavaḥ sarṣapāram ||
4.d: त्रयस्त्रिहायणीवालाः सर्षपार्धं विधीयते द्विगुणं सर्षपं प्राहुर्यवः सर्षपारम् ॥
4.m:
Three hairs of a three-year-old [heifer] are ordained as half a mustard seed;

Double [that] they call a mustard seed; a barleycorn is [...] mustard seeds. \3\

4.s: aṅgulasya pramāṇaṃ tu ṣaḍyavāḥ pārśvasaṃhitāḥ daśāṅgulastu prādeśo vitastirdvādaśāṅgulaḥ dvivitastiraratniḥ syādvyāyāmastu catuḥśayaḥ ||
4.d: अङ्गुलस्य प्रमाणं तु षड्यवाः पार्श्वसंहिताः दशाङ्गुलस्तु प्रादेशो वितस्तिर्द्वादशाङ्गुलः द्विवितस्तिररत्निः स्याद्व्यायामस्तु चतुःशयः ॥

4.s: viṃśatiśatāṅgulataḥ puruṣaḥ svaiḥ svairaṅguliparvabhiḥ atha cetprapadotthānaḥ pañcaviṃśaśato bhavet ||
4.d: विंशतिशताङ्गुलतः पुरुषः स्वैः स्वैरङ्गुलिपर्वभिः अथ चेत्प्रपदोत्थानः पञ्चविंशशतो भवेत् ॥
4.m:
The man-length is one hundred and twenty finger-breadths by [the sacrificer's] own finger-joints;

if he stands on tiptoe, it should be one hundred and twenty-five. // 5

4.s: triyavaṃ kṛṣṇalaṃ vidyāt mānaṃ vidyāt trikṛṣṇalam anena kṛṣṇalapramāṇena niṣkamāhuścaturguṇam ||
4.d: त्रियवं कृष्णलं विद्यात् मानं विद्यात् त्रिकृष्णलम् अनेन कृष्णलप्रमाणेन निष्कमाहुश्चतुर्गुणम् ॥
4.m:
One should know a kṛṣṇala as three barleycorns; one should know a measure [māṣa] as three kṛṣṇalas;

by this measure of kṛṣṇalas, they say a niṣka is fourfold [that]. // 6

4.s: puruṣasya tṛtīyapañcamau bhāgau tatkaraṇaṃ punaściteḥ tasyārdhamathāparaṃ bhavettricitikamagnicitiścet ||
4.d: पुरुषस्य तृतीयपञ्चमौ भागौ तत्करणं पुनश्चितेः तस्यार्धमथापरं भवेत्त्रिचितिकमग्निचितिश्चेत् ॥
4.m:
The third and fifth parts of a man-length are the producing sides for the piling again;

half of it then should be another; if it is an altar piling of three brick layers. // 7

4.s: aṣṭāvaṣṭau saṃmitā citiraṣṭaikādaśikā ca madhyamā vyatyā savatīrupanyasedaṣṭau dvādaśa cottamā citiḥ ||
4.d: अष्टावष्टौ संमिता चितिरष्टैकादशिका च मध्यमा व्यत्या सवतीरुपन्यसेदष्टौ द्वादश चोत्तमा चितिः ॥
4.m:
The brick layer is measured as eight by eight, and the middle one as eight by eleven;

he should lay them alternating, and the uppermost brick layer is eight by twelve. // 8 // (4)

5.m: Now next we will explain the northern brick [piling]. // 1
He measures out a bamboo rod by the sacrificer with arms raised. // 2

5.d: तत्समो ऽन्यतरः सारत्निर्द्वितीयस्तस्य पुरुषे लक्षणमरत्नि वितस्त्योश्चोभयोरर्धपुरुषे ॥
5.m: The other is equal to that, [and] a second is with a cubit; on it, there is a mark at a man-length, and on both, at a cubit, a span, [and] half a man-length. // 3

5.s: śirasi pariśrite yūpāyāvaśiṣya śeṣamanurajju puruṣau saṃdhāya pañcāṅgyā śaṅkuṃ vinihanti tayoḥ saṃdhāvardhayośca ||
5.d: शिरसि परिश्रिते यूपायावशिष्य शेषमनुरज्जु पुरुषौ संधाय पञ्चाङ्ग्या शङ्कुं विनिहन्ति तयोः संधावर्धयोश्च ॥
5.m: When the head is enclosed, leaving space for the sacrificial post, having joined two man-lengths along the cord, he drives a peg with the five-marked cord at their junction and at their halves. // 4

5.s: yāvabhito madhyamaṃ śaṅkuṃ tayorveṇū nidyāya dakṣiṇataḥ puruṣasaṃnipāte todaṃ karoti ||
5.d: यावभितो मध्यमं शङ्कुं तयोर्वेणू निद्याय दक्षिणतः पुरुषसंनिपाते तोदं करोति ॥
5.m: Having placed the two bamboo rods on the two [pegs] on both sides of the middle peg, he makes a pointer at the intersection of a man-length to the south. // 5

5.s: madhyame śaṅkau veṇuṃ nidhāyādhyadhi todaṃ hṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ puruṣe śaṅkuṃ nihanti ||
5.d: मध्यमे शङ्कौ वेणुं निधायाध्यधि तोदं हृत्वा दक्षिणतः पुरुषे शङ्कुं निहन्ति ॥
5.m: Having placed a bamboo rod on the middle peg and drawn the pointer directly over, he drives a peg to the south at a man-length. // 6

5.s: pūrve śaṅkau veṇuṃ nidhāya dvitīyaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ purastātpuruṣasaṃnipāte śaṅkuṃ nihantyardhe caivaṃ paścāt ||
5.d: पूर्वे शङ्कौ वेणुं निधाय द्वितीयं दक्षिणतः पुरस्तात्पुरुषसंनिपाते शङ्कुं निहन्त्यर्धे चैवं पश्चात् ॥
5.m: Having placed a bamboo rod on the eastern peg, [and] the second to the south, he drives a peg at the intersection of a man-length in front, and likewise behind at the half. // 7
By this, the northern half is explained. // 8

5.s: dakṣiṇasya vargasya yāvabhito madhyamaṃ śaṅkuṃ tayorveṇū nidhāya dakṣiṇataḥ puruṣasaṃnipāte todaṃ karoti ||
5.d: दक्षिणस्य वर्गस्य यावभितो मध्यमं शङ्कुं तयोर्वेणू निधाय दक्षिणतः पुरुषसंनिपाते तोदं करोति ॥
5.m: Having placed the two bamboo rods on the two [pegs] on both sides of the middle peg of the southern group, he makes a pointer at the intersection of a man-length to the south. // 9

5.s: madhyame śaṅkau veṇuṃ nidhāyādhyapi todaṃ hṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ sāratnau śaṅkuṃ nihanti ||
5.d: मध्यमे शङ्कौ वेणुं निधायाध्यपि तोदं हृत्वा दक्षिणतः सारत्नौ शङ्कुं निहन्ति ॥
5.m: Having placed a bamboo rod on the middle peg and drawn the pointer directly over, he drives a peg to the south at [the mark] with a cubit. // 10

5.s: yaḥ sāratnistaṃ madhyamasya pūrve nidhāya dvitīyaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ purastātsāratnimardhapuruṣeṇa saṃnipātya śaṅkuṃ nihantyevaṃ paścāt ||
5.d: यः सारत्निस्तं मध्यमस्य पूर्वे निधाय द्वितीयं दक्षिणतः पुरस्तात्सारत्निमर्धपुरुषेण संनिपात्य शङ्कुं निहन्त्येवं पश्चात् ॥
5.m: Having placed the one with a cubit to the east of the middle one, [and] the second to the south, having brought [it] with half a man-length to meet the one with a cubit in front, he drives a peg, and likewise behind. // 11
By this very method, the northern wing is explained. // 12
The tail has a span in place of the cubit. // 13
He measures out the head in front of the eastern [peg] with half a man-length by means of the five-marked cord. // 14 // (5)

6.s: vyāyāmasyāṣṭamamekatasturīyamekata ubhayatasturīyaṃ ca te gārhapatyaciteḥ karaṇe ||
6.d: व्यायामस्याष्टममेकतस्तुरीयमेकत उभयतस्तुरीयं च ते गार्हपत्यचितेः करणे ॥
6.m: An eighth [part] of a fathom on one side and a fourth on the other, and a fourth on both sides: those are the producing sides of the Gārhapatya piling. // 1

6.s: puruṣasya daśamena bhāgena prathamaṃ caturaśraṃ karaṇaṃ kārayeddaśamamekato 'rdhamekatastaddvitīyaṃ daśamamekato 'dhyardhamekatastattṛtīyamubhayatasturīyaṃ taccaturtham ||
6.d: पुरुषस्य दशमेन भागेन प्रथमं चतुरश्रं करणं कारयेद्दशममेकतो ऽर्धमेकतस्तद्द्वितीयं दशममेकतो ऽध्यर्धमेकतस्तत्तृतीयमुभयतस्तुरीयं तच्चतुर्थम् ॥
6.m: He should have the first square producing side made with a tenth part of a man-length; a tenth on one side and a half on the other is the second; a tenth on one side and one and a half on the other is the third; a fourth on both sides is the fourth. // 2

6.s: tāsāmutsedhastriṃśatpañcamabhāgenānyatra nākasadbhyaśca cūḍābhya ṛtavyābhyo 'tha madhyamāyāṃ pañcamaṣaṣṭhībhyaśca vaiśvadevībhyastā ardhotsedhāḥ ||
6.d: तासामुत्सेधस्त्रिंशत्पञ्चमभागेनान्यत्र नाकसद्भ्यश्च चूडाभ्य ऋतव्याभ्यो ऽथ मध्यमायां पञ्चमषष्ठीभ्यश्च वैश्वदेवीभ्यस्ता अर्धोत्सेधाः ॥
6.m: Their height is thirty-fifth parts, except for the Nākasads, the Cūḍās, and the Ṛtavyās; and in the middle [layer], the fifth and sixth Vaiśvadevī bricks: these are half-height. // 3
Having put earth in between, he should lay the next layer, for connection of the group and for non-interruption. // 4
In pits he should deposit whatever is other than bricks. // 5

6.s: tatra śloko bhavati ukhāyāḥ paśuśīrṣāṇāṃ kūrmasyolūkhalasya ca srucoḥ kumbheṣṭakānāṃ ca caroścaivāvaṭānkhanet ||
6.d: तत्र श्लोको भवति उखायाः पशुशीर्षाणां कूर्मस्योलूखलस्य च स्रुचोः कुम्भेष्टकानां च चरोश्चैवावटान्खनेत् ॥
6.m: There is a verse on this: / One should dig pits for the pot, the animal heads, the tortoise, the mortar, / the two offering ladles, the pot-bricks, and the boiled-grain mess. // 6

6.s: pratidiśamupadadhyādātmani madhye prācīḥ śirasi pucche pakṣayoścātmanyapyayeṣu samaṃ vibhajyottarāmuttarāmapyayasaṃhitāṃ pūrvāparadakṣiṇottarā viṣayavacanādanyaccatasraḥ purastātpañcartavyābhyaḥ paścāccottarapūrve cārdhe gārhapatyasya | śeṣaṃ caturaśrābhiḥ ||
6.d: प्रतिदिशमुपदध्यादात्मनि मध्ये प्राचीः शिरसि पुच्छे पक्षयोश्चात्मन्यप्ययेषु समं विभज्योत्तरामुत्तरामप्ययसंहितां पूर्वापरदक्षिणोत्तरा विषयवचनादन्यच्चतस्रः पुरस्तात्पञ्चर्तव्याभ्यः पश्चाच्चोत्तरपूर्वे चार्धे गार्हपत्यस्य । शेषं चतुरश्राभिः ॥
6.m: He should lay [bricks] facing each direction: in the body, in the middle, facing east, in the head, in the tail, and in the two wings, and in the body joints, dividing equally, laying layer after layer joined at the joints, facing east-west, south-north, unless otherwise specified; four in front and five behind the Ṛtavyās, and in the northeast half of the Gārhapatya; the rest with square [bricks]. // 7

6.s: etā eva dakṣiṇottarā dvitīyasyāṃ | śeṣaṃ caturaśrābhiḥ ||
6.d: एता एव दक्षिणोत्तरा द्वितीयस्यां । शेषं चतुरश्राभिः ॥
6.m: These very ones [facing] south-north in the second [layer]; the rest with square [bricks]. // 8

6.s: yathā prathamaivaṃ tṛtīyā pañcamī vā yathā dvitīyaivaṃ caturthe | tena dharmena vatyāsaṃ cinuyāt ||
6.d: यथा प्रथमैवं तृतीया पञ्चमी वा यथा द्वितीयैवं चतुर्थे । तेन धर्मेन वत्यासं चिनुयात् ॥
6.m: As the first, so the third or fifth; as the second, so the fourth; according to that rule, he should pile with alternation. // 9

6.s: athetarānāgnīdhrīyādīn navanava padāni karotyekaikaṃ madhye 'smānamāgnīdhrīye | catvāri catvāri turīyāṇi pratidiśaṃ hotrīye | catasro 'rdhāḥ kuṣṭhāsu brāhyaṇāchaṃsya | itareṣāṃ dve dve adhyardhe madhye prācīḥ | ṣaḍeva mārjālīye paśusrapaṇe ca ||
6.d: अथेतरानाग्नीध्रीयादीन् नवनव पदानि करोत्येकैकं मध्ये ऽस्मानमाग्नीध्रीये । चत्वारि चत्वारि तुरीयाणि प्रतिदिशं होत्रीये । चतस्रो ऽर्धाः कुष्ठासु ब्राह्यणाछंस्य । इतरेषां द्वे द्वे अध्यर्धे मध्ये प्राचीः । षडेव मार्जालीये पशुस्रपणे च ॥
6.m: Then, the other [fireplaces] beginning with the Āgnīdhra, he makes nine feet each; in the Āgnīdhra, one stone in the middle; four fourth-bricks facing each direction in the Hotṛ's fireplace; four half-bricks at the sides in the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's fireplace; in the others, two one-and-a-half bricks in the middle facing east; six only in the Mārjālīya and the animal-cooking [hearth]. // 10

6.s: viṃśatimadhyardhāḥ prācīraṃsayordadyācchroṇyoḥ pucche ca viṃśatiṃ dvādaśa dvādaśa purastātpakṣayoḥ prācīḥ paścācca pañca pañca codīcīrabhitaḥ śirasi | śeṣaṃ caturaśrābhiḥ ||
6.d: विंशतिमध्यर्धाः प्राचीरंसयोर्दद्याच्छ्रोण्योः पुच्छे च विंशतिं द्वादश द्वादश पुरस्तात्पक्षयोः प्राचीः पश्चाच्च पञ्च पञ्च चोदीचीरभितः शिरसि । शेषं चतुरश्राभिः ॥
6.m: He should place twenty one-and-a-half bricks facing east on the two shoulders, and twenty on the two buttocks and the tail; twelve facing east in front and behind on each of the two wings; and five facing north on both sides in the head; the rest with square [bricks]. // 11

6.s: viṃśatiṃ śroṇyaṃsapakṣeṣaūdīcīrdakṣiṇatastathottarato dvitīyasyāmekādaśaikādaśābhitaḥ pucche pañca pañca prācīrabhitaḥ śirase | śeṣaṃ caturaśrābhiḥ ||
6.d: विंशतिं श्रोण्यंसपक्षेषऊदीचीर्दक्षिणतस्तथोत्तरतो द्वितीयस्यामेकादशैकादशाभितः पुच्छे पञ्च पञ्च प्राचीरभितः शिरसे । शेषं चतुरश्राभिः ॥
6.m: Twenty facing north on the buttocks, shoulders, and wings, to the south and likewise to the north in the second [layer]; eleven on each side in the tail; five facing east on both sides in the head; the rest with square [bricks]. // 12

6.s: yathā prathamaivaṃ tṛtīyā pañcamī ca yathā dvitīyaivaṃ caturthyetena dharmeṇa vyatyāsaṃ cinuyāt ||
6.d: यथा प्रथमैवं तृतीया पञ्चमी च यथा द्वितीयैवं चतुर्थ्येतेन धर्मेण व्यत्यासं चिनुयात् ॥
6.m: As the first, so the third and fifth; as the second, so the fourth; according to this rule, he should pile with alternation. // 13

6.s: trirupasatsu dve pūrvasyāṃ tisro madhyamāyāṃ ṣaṭsu yathānupūrveṇa dvādaśasu vyatyāsaṃ citipurīṣe karoti ||
6.d: त्रिरुपसत्सु द्वे पूर्वस्यां तिस्रो मध्यमायां षट्सु यथानुपूर्वेण द्वादशसु व्यत्यासं चितिपुरीषे करोति ॥
6.m: When there are three Upasads, [he lays] two in the first [layer] and three in the middle; when there are six, in order; when there are twelve, he makes alternation in the brick layers and earth. // 14

6.s: etena dharmeṇa saṃvatsarātsamaṃ vibhajya jānudaghne 'sya dviguṇaṃ triguṇamuttareṣāṃ caikāmuttarāmuddhatyābhyāyanaṃ vardhāyātiriktā upadadhyāt ||
6.d: एतेन धर्मेण संवत्सरात्समं विभज्य जानुदघ्ने ऽस्य द्विगुणं त्रिगुणमुत्तरेषां चैकामुत्तरामुद्धत्याभ्यायनं वर्धायातिरिक्ता उपदध्यात् ॥
6.m: According to this rule, dividing equally after a year, at knee-height of this, [or] double, [or] triple; and lifting up one upper layer of the subsequent ones, he should lay the excess [bricks] to increase the growth. // 15
Beginning with the mantra and ending with the touching, that is the mark of the man-length. // 16 // (6)

7.s: darbhastambaṃ puṣkaraparṇaṃ rukmapuruṣau hiraṇyeṣṭakāṃ śarkarāṃ svayamātṛṇṇāṃ dūrveṣṭakā naivāramiti madhyaṃ | tasminkumbheṣṭakā yā madhye dakṣiṇottare ca srucāvanūpamadhyeṣu śeṣāḥ | paścātsvayamātṛṇṇāyāḥ kulāyinīṃ dviyajuśca vaṃśayoḥ pārśvasaṃhite dviyajuruttare purastādretaḥsicau dve | dakṣiṇe tasminvaṃśe dvitīyāmṛtavyāṃ ca purastāccaturthe loke retaḥsicaṃ viśvajyotiṣaṃ maṇḍalāmṛtavyāṃ gharmeṣṭakāmaṣāḍhāṃ kūrmaṃ vṛṣabhamiti prāñcamuttare vaṃśe dakṣiṇataḥ purastātsvayamātṛṇṇāyāḥ pañca mulūkhalamusalamuttarapūrve cokhāṃ madhye śirasāṃ śirobhiḥ saṃhitāmupadadhāti ||
7.d: दर्भस्तम्बं पुष्करपर्णं रुक्मपुरुषौ हिरण्येष्टकां शर्करां स्वयमातृण्णां दूर्वेष्टका नैवारमिति मध्यं । तस्मिन्कुम्भेष्टका या मध्ये दक्षिणोत्तरे च स्रुचावनूपमध्येषु शेषाः । पश्चात्स्वयमातृण्णायाः कुलायिनीं द्वियजुश्च वंशयोः पार्श्वसंहिते द्वियजुरुत्तरे पुरस्ताद्रेतःसिचौ द्वे । दक्षिणे तस्मिन्वंशे द्वितीयामृतव्यां च पुरस्ताच्चतुर्थे लोके रेतःसिचं विश्वज्योतिषं मण्डलामृतव्यां घर्मेष्टकामषाढां कूर्मं वृषभमिति प्राञ्चमुत्तरे वंशे दक्षिणतः पुरस्तात्स्वयमातृण्णायाः पञ्च मुलूखलमुसलमुत्तरपूर्वे चोखां मध्ये शिरसां शिरोभिः संहितामुपदधाति ॥
7.m: A clump of darbha grass, a lotus leaf, a golden man, a gold brick, gravel, a naturally perforated brick, a dūrvā brick, wild rice: this is the center; in it, the pot-bricks which are in the middle, and to the south and north, two ladles; the remaining ones along the middle; behind the naturally perforated brick, the kulāyinī and the two-yajuṣ brick on the two axial lines, joined at the sides; the two-yajuṣ in the north, two libation-pourers in front; on that southern axial line, the second Ṛtavyā; and in front in the fourth space, a libation-pourer, the Viśvajyotis, a circular Ṛtavyā, a Gharma brick, an Aṣāḍhā, a tortoise, a bull, facing east; on the northern axial line to the south in front of the naturally perforated brick, five; the mortar and pestle in the northeast, and the pot in the middle joined with the heads of the [sacrificial] heads he deposits. // 1

7.s: tasyāḥ paścātpuruṣaśirasaḥ puruṣacitimupadadhāti ṣaṭtriṃśataṃ pratīcīstrivargeṇa śroṇyām ||
7.d: तस्याः पश्चात्पुरुषशिरसः पुरुषचितिमुपदधाति षट्त्रिंशतं प्रतीचीस्त्रिवर्गेण श्रोण्याम् ॥
7.m: Behind it, he lays a man-piling of the man's head, thirty-six facing west, in a triad on the buttock. // 2

7.s: tatra śloko bhavati tisro grīvāḥ ṣaḍaṃsayordve dve bāhvornavātmani jaṅghayoru pañca paścādasmānāmekaikaṃ pāṇipādayoḥ ||
7.d: तत्र श्लोको भवति तिस्रो ग्रीवाः षडंसयोर्द्वे द्वे बाह्वोर्नवात्मनि जङ्घयोरु पञ्च पश्चादस्मानामेकैकं पाणिपादयोः ॥
7.m:
Three on the neck, six on the two shoulders, two on each of the two arms, nine on the torso,

five on each of the two thighs behind, and one stone on each of the hands and feet. // 3

7.s: aṣṭavathāpasyāḥ samaṃ vibhajya vaṃśeṣu navamenavame prāṇabhṛtaḥ purastāduttare vaṃśe prathamaṃ paścāddakṣiṇe dakṣiṇataḥ pūrva uttarataḥ paścāddakṣiṇataḥ svayamātṛṇṇāyā dvitīye pañcamamanūpeṣu saṃyato navame 'timātrā yathā prāṇabhṛtaḥ purastāddakṣiṇe vaṃśe prathamaṃ paścāduttare dakṣiṇataḥ paścāduttarataḥ pūrva uttarataḥ paścāddakṣiṇataḥ uttarataḥ svayamātṛṇṇāyā dvitīye pañcamam | vaiśvadevyaścānūpeṣu pratidiśamuttarapūrveṣu vaṃśeṣvādyā | dakṣiṇottare ca saṃyānyāvapyaye tayorvaṃśayorādyāt purastādvātharvaśiraḥ ||
7.d: अष्टवथापस्याः समं विभज्य वंशेषु नवमेनवमे प्राणभृतः पुरस्तादुत्तरे वंशे प्रथमं पश्चाद्दक्षिणे दक्षिणतः पूर्व उत्तरतः पश्चाद्दक्षिणतः स्वयमातृण्णाया द्वितीये पञ्चममनूपेषु संयतो नवमे ऽतिमात्रा यथा प्राणभृतः पुरस्ताद्दक्षिणे वंशे प्रथमं पश्चादुत्तरे दक्षिणतः पश्चादुत्तरतः पूर्व उत्तरतः पश्चाद्दक्षिणतः उत्तरतः स्वयमातृण्णाया द्वितीये पञ्चमम् । वैश्वदेव्यश्चानूपेषु प्रतिदिशमुत्तरपूर्वेषु वंशेष्वाद्या । दक्षिणोत्तरे च संयान्यावप्यये तयोर्वंशयोराद्यात् पुरस्ताद्वाथर्वशिरः ॥
7.m: Now, having divided the apasyā bricks equally among the structural lines, [one lays] the prāṇabhṛt bricks on every ninth [mark]: first on the northern line in front, then on the southern behind, to the south in front, to the north behind, to the south of the svayamātṛṇṇā brick; on the second [layer, one places] the fifth in the marshy spaces, together on the ninth. The atimātrā bricks are [laid] like the prāṇabhṛt bricks: first on the southern line in front, then on the northern behind, to the south behind, to the north in front, to the north behind, to the south; to the north of the svayamātṛṇṇā brick, on the second [layer, one places] the fifth. And the vaiśvadevī bricks [are placed] in the marshy spaces, in each direction, the first ones on the north-eastern lines; and the two saṃyānī bricks at the southern and northern conjunction; or rather, from the first of those two lines in front, the Atharvaśiras brick.

7.s: samaṃ vibhajya vaṃśeṣu śiraḥ pakṣapucchāni prathameṣu vaṃśeṣu lokānvijānīyāt ||
7.d: समं विभज्य वंशेषु शिरः पक्षपुच्छानि प्रथमेषु वंशेषु लोकान्विजानीयात् ॥
7.m: Having divided [the spaces] equally among the structural lines, one should understand the head, wings, and tail [to lie] on the first lines as spaces.

7.s: śirasi prathame vaṃśa uttarāmuttarāmitareṣāṃ pakṣapucchānāṃ caturthe pakṣayoḥ prācīḥ pucche codīcīrlokeṣṭakā upadadhyāccheṣāḥ paścātsvayamātṛṇṇāyā ekaikaṃ pūrvaṃ saṃhitām | dakṣiṇe vaṃśe vaiśvadevyādya uttare ca purīṣādyāḥ ||
7.d: शिरसि प्रथमे वंश उत्तरामुत्तरामितरेषां पक्षपुच्छानां चतुर्थे पक्षयोः प्राचीः पुच्छे चोदीचीर्लोकेष्टका उपदध्याच्छेषाः पश्चात्स्वयमातृण्णाया एकैकं पूर्वं संहिताम् । दक्षिणे वंशे वैश्वदेव्याद्य उत्तरे च पुरीषाद्याः ॥
7.m: On the head, along the first structural line, [one places] further and further [bricks]; along the fourth of the other wings and tail, one should lay space-filler bricks pointing east on the wings and pointing north on the tail; the remaining [space-filler bricks are placed] behind the svayamātṛṇṇā brick, one by one, joined to the front; on the southern line, beginning with the vaiśvadevī bricks, and on the north, beginning with the loose earth bricks.

7.s: gāyatraṃ madhye śirasi rathantaraṃ bṛhadyajñāyamiti yathāmnātam ||
7.d: गायत्रं मध्ये शिरसि रथन्तरं बृहद्यज्ञायमिति यथाम्नातम् ॥
7.m: The Gāyatra brick is in the middle of the head; the Rathantara, Bṛhat, and Yajñāyajñīya bricks are [laid] according to the sacred tradition. (7)

8.s: dvitīyāyāṃ purastātsvayamātṛṇṇāyāḥ prathamadvitīyatṛtīyeṣvṛtavyā vāyavyā apasyā iti yathāsaṃkhyam | tisrastisro dakṣiṇeṣu vaṃśeṣu dakṣiṇottarā dve dve uttarasyottarayornavame 'bhitaḥ śeṣā yathāpasyāḥ ||
8.d: द्वितीयायां पुरस्तात्स्वयमातृण्णायाः प्रथमद्वितीयतृतीयेष्वृतव्या वायव्या अपस्या इति यथासंख्यम् । तिस्रस्तिस्रो दक्षिणेषु वंशेषु दक्षिणोत्तरा द्वे द्वे उत्तरस्योत्तरयोर्नवमे ऽभितः शेषा यथापस्याः ॥
8.m: In the second [layer], in front of the svayamātṛṇṇā brick, on the first, second, and third [lines, one places] the ṛtavyā, vāyavyā, and apasyā bricks respectively; three each on the southern lines, extending south to north; two each on the two northern lines of the northern [part]; on the ninth [line] on both sides, the remainder [are laid] like the apasyā bricks.

8.s: tṛtīyāyāṃ daśa dvādaśa navame 'abhito | aṣṭame sapta purastātpaścācca samīcīrabhitaḥ svayamātṛṇṇāyā ardhotsedhā aṣṭau nānāmantrā uttamāyāṃ vā ||
8.d: तृतीयायां दश द्वादश नवमे ऽअभितो । अष्टमे सप्त पुरस्तात्पश्चाच्च समीचीरभितः स्वयमातृण्णाया अर्धोत्सेधा अष्टौ नानामन्त्रा उत्तमायां वा ॥
8.m: In the third [layer, one places] ten [and] twelve on both sides of the ninth; on the eighth, seven in front and behind facing one another around the svayamātṛṇṇā brick; eight of half-height with distinct mantras, or in the uppermost layer.

8.s: caturthyāmekaikāṃ navamenavame 'bhitaḥ purastāduttarasya vaṃśasya madhye prathamāṃ vyatyāsamitarā | evameva spṛtaḥ purastāddakṣiṇasya vaṃśasya madhye prathamāṃ vyatyāsamitarāḥ | ṣaṭsaptāṣṭameṣu dakṣiṇato yugmāyugmā uttaratastrivargānkuryātsaptadaśa dakṣiṇataḥ pañcadaśottarataḥ ||
8.d: चतुर्थ्यामेकैकां नवमेनवमे ऽभितः पुरस्तादुत्तरस्य वंशस्य मध्ये प्रथमां व्यत्यासमितरा । एवमेव स्पृतः पुरस्ताद्दक्षिणस्य वंशस्य मध्ये प्रथमां व्यत्यासमितराः । षट्सप्ताष्टमेषु दक्षिणतो युग्मायुग्मा उत्तरतस्त्रिवर्गान्कुर्यात्सप्तदश दक्षिणतः पञ्चदशोत्तरतः ॥
8.m: In the fourth [layer, one places] one on both sides on every ninth [mark]; the first in the middle of the northern line in front, the others alternately; just so the spṛt bricks: the first in the middle of the southern line in front, the others alternately; on the sixth, seventh, and eighth [lines], one should make pairs and non-pairs to the south, and sets of three to the north: seventeen to the south, fifteen to the north.

8.s: pañcamyāmekaikāṃ prāṇabhṛdādhiṣu śeṣaṃ chandasāṃ virājaśca yathātimātrāḥ ṣaṭsaptāṣṭameṣvabhito yathāsaṃkhyam ||
8.d: पञ्चम्यामेकैकां प्राणभृदाधिषु शेषं छन्दसां विराजश्च यथातिमात्राः षट्सप्ताष्टमेष्वभितो यथासंख्यम् ॥
8.m: In the fifth [layer, one places] one on each [spot] beginning with the prāṇabhṛt bricks; the remainder of the metres and the virāj bricks [are placed] like the atimātrā bricks on the sixth, seventh, and eighth [lines] on both sides, respectively.

8.s: ardheṣṭakābhiḥ pūrayitvā dakṣiṇataḥ prācīḥ stomabhāgāḥ paścimāśca yugmā uttaratastrivargānkuryādekatriṃśatam | paścātpratyañcaṃ trivargeṇa nākasadaṃ ca paścātpurīṣavatyā yavādinā sanāmnīrupaśīvarīrghṛtaplutā iti yathāsaṃkhyam | turīyāṇi madhye yathā prāṇabhṛto 'timātrā madhyamāṃ svayamātṛṇṇāsaṃhitāmuttarastu vikarṇīm ||
8.d: अर्धेष्टकाभिः पूरयित्वा दक्षिणतः प्राचीः स्तोमभागाः पश्चिमाश्च युग्मा उत्तरतस्त्रिवर्गान्कुर्यादेकत्रिंशतम् । पश्चात्प्रत्यञ्चं त्रिवर्गेण नाकसदं च पश्चात्पुरीषवत्या यवादिना सनाम्नीरुपशीवरीर्घृतप्लुता इति यथासंख्यम् । तुरीयाणि मध्ये यथा प्राणभृतो ऽतिमात्रा मध्यमां स्वयमातृण्णासंहितामुत्तरस्तु विकर्णीम् ॥
8.m: Having filled [the gaps] with half-bricks, [one places] the stomabhāgā bricks pointing east to the south; and to the west, pairs; to the north, one should make sets of three, [totaling] thirty-one; behind, westward, with a set of three; and behind, the nākasad brick; behind the loose-earth brick, the [bricks named] yavādī, sanāmnī, upaśīvarī, and ghṛtaplutā respectively; quarter-bricks in the middle like the prāṇabhṛt bricks; the atimātrā brick in the middle contiguous to the svayamātṛṇṇā brick, but the vikarṇī brick to the north.

9.s: yāvatī śoṣapākābhyāmiṣṭakā hrasate kṛtā tāvatsamadhikaṃ kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ samamicchata ||
9.d: यावती शोषपाकाभ्यामिष्टका ह्रसते कृता तावत्समधिकं कार्यं करणं सममिच्छत ॥
9.m:
By as much as a brick, once made, shrinks through drying and baking,

by that much larger should the mould be made by one who desires equality.

9.s: sadā ca triṃśakaṃ bhāgamiṣṭakā hrasate kṛtā tāvat samadhikaṃ kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ samamicchata ||
9.d: सदा च त्रिंशकं भागमिष्टका ह्रसते कृता तावत् समधिकं कार्यं करणं सममिच्छत ॥
9.m:
And a brick, once made, constantly shrinks by a thirtieth part;

by that much larger should the mould be made by one who desires equality.

9.s: ekaikaṃ śatamadhyardhaṃ tadūtaṃ ṣaḍabhiraṅgulaiḥ iṣṭakānāṃ parimāṇaṃ vaikṛtaṃ yadato 'nyathā ||
9.d: एकैकं शतमध्यर्धं तदूतं षडभिरङ्गुलैः इष्टकानां परिमाणं वैकृतं यदतो ऽन्यथा ॥
9.m:
One hundred and fifty [aṅgulas] each, minus six finger-breadths: / that is the measure of the bricks; any other than this is modified.

Nine thousand two hundred and sixteen finger-breadths / is specified as the measure of the finger-breadths of the vyāyāma.

9.s: navāṅgulasahasrāṇi dve śate ṣoḍaśottare aṅgulānāṃ parimāṇaṃ vyāyāmasya tu nirdiśet ||
9.d: नवाङ्गुलसहस्राणि द्वे शते षोडशोत्तरे अङ्गुलानां परिमाणं व्यायामस्य तु निर्दिशेत् ॥
9.m:
However, for all the other dhiṣṇya hearths, the determination is: / for each one there shall be one thousand one hundred and ninety-six [square finger-breadths].

Eleven thousand six hundred finger-breadths, / and indeed one hundred thousand: [such] is prescribed as the area of the fire-altar.

9.s: itareṣāṃ tu dhiṣṇyānāṃ sarveṣāmeva niścayaḥ ekaikasya sahasraṃ syācchate ṣaṇṇavatiḥ parā ||
9.d: इतरेषां तु धिष्ण्यानां सर्वेषामेव निश्चयः एकैकस्य सहस्रं स्याच्छते षण्णवतिः परा ॥
9.m:
Whether the primary or the modified [fire-altar], whose area is seven and a half [square puruṣas], / having made the head twenty-five [square feet], one should then deposit it in the area.

Eight hundred feet less a foot are proclaimed here [as the area]; / the knowers of areas know the area of [the altar] with its limbs and head.

9.s: ekādaśa sahasrāṇi aṅgulānāṃ śatāni ṣaṭ śataṃ caiva sahasrāṇāṃ kṣetramagnervidhīyate ||
9.d: एकादश सहस्राणि अङ्गुलानां शतानि षट् शतं चैव सहस्राणां क्षेत्रमग्नेर्विधीयते ॥
9.m:
The body should be made four hundred [feet]; the two wings are known as one hundred and thirty [each]; / one hundred and ten in the tail, and the head should be twenty-five [feet].

By groups of thirty-one, thirty-three, / and also by groups of fifty, / when groups do not fit, a brick should be divided in two.

9.s: prākṛtaṃ vaikṛtaṃ vāpi kṣetramardhāṣṭamāntare pañcaviṃśaṃ śiraḥ kṛtvā tataḥ kṣetre samāvapet ||
9.d: प्राकृतं वैकृतं वापि क्षेत्रमर्धाष्टमान्तरे पञ्चविंशं शिरः कृत्वा ततः क्षेत्रे समावपेत् ॥
9.m:
By the shrinking and enlarging of bricks, among the solid ones and in sets of hundreds, / the wise person should adjust the bricks into parts according to the mantras.

On the square or on the spine, the bricks of the wings, tail, and head / are laid according to direction and according to space, and thus no space is lost.

9.s: śatānyaṣṭau padonāni padānāmiha kīrtyante sāṅgasya saśiraskasya kṣetraṃ kṣetravido viduḥ ||
9.d: शतान्यष्टौ पदोनानि पदानामिह कीर्त्यन्ते साङ्गस्य सशिरस्कस्य क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रविदो विदुः ॥
9.m:
The laying [of the bricks] upon the body should indeed be known by the knowledgeable one: / another with the Rathantara and Bṛhat spaces, [and another] with the Gāyatra and Yājñiya [spaces].

The count of all the bricks accompanied by mantras is fixed; / hear from me as I declare that [count] in each brick layer:

9.s: ātmā catuḥśataḥ kāryaḥ pakṣau triṃśacchatau smṛtau daśa pucche śataṃ caiva śiraḥ syāt pañcaviṃśakam ||
9.d: आत्मा चतुःशतः कार्यः पक्षौ त्रिंशच्छतौ स्मृतौ दश पुच्छे शतं चैव शिरः स्यात् पञ्चविंशकम् ॥
9.m:
The first [layer has] one hundred and eighty-six; the second, one hundred and seventy; / the third should be one hundred and thirteen, so the wise say;

the fourth is known to have one hundred and one, plus three bricks; / and three hundred and fifty-six [is] the highest brick layer.

9.s: ekatriṃśastrayastriṃśairvargaiḥ pañcāśakairapi asaṃbhavatsu vargeṣu dvidhā bhidyeta iṣṭakā ||
9.d: एकत्रिंशस्त्रयस्त्रिंशैर्वर्गैः पञ्चाशकैरपि असंभवत्सु वर्गेषु द्विधा भिद्येत इष्टका ॥
9.m:
All these are bricks accompanied by mantras, with which the fire-altar is brought forth; / but one should fill up the rest of the brick layers with space-filler bricks.

All these are recited in the sacred tradition, as far as the Yajurveda extends; / this indeed amounts to a thousand, spoken of together with the potsherds.

9.s: iṣṭakāhrāsavṛddhibhyāṃ dṛḍhāsu śatakeṣu ca matimāniṣṭakā bhāgairmantrātsaṃnāśayediti ||
9.d: इष्टकाह्रासवृद्धिभ्यां दृढासु शतकेषु च मतिमानिष्टका भागैर्मन्त्रात्संनाशयेदिति ॥
9.m:
These bricks, properly laid, indeed become milch cows; / they yield all desires for the sacrificer in the other world.

Whoever knows Prajāpati [as having] sixty [parts], which is known as the year, / goes to the world of Brahman, to the highest vault of the sun. (9)

9.s: caturaśre pṛṣṭau vāpi pakṣapucchaśireṣṭakāḥ dikto 'padhānaṃ lokācca tathā lokastu lupyate ||
9.d: चतुरश्रे पृष्टौ वापि पक्षपुच्छशिरेष्टकाः दिक्तो ऽपधानं लोकाच्च तथा लोकस्तु लुप्यते ॥
9.m:
To that [altar] belonging to Viṣṇu, to be measured in every way by the knowers of the cord, / to the reckoners and the teachers, paying homage, we who meditate:

We partake of this earth which, like a measurer for us, / [provides] the sacrificial, supreme measure, prospering in one's own home.

9.s: adhyātmani ha vijñeyamupadhānaṃ vijānatā rathantarabṛhallokairanyaṃ gāyatrayājñiyaiḥ ||
9.d: अध्यात्मनि ह विज्ञेयमुपधानं विजानता रथन्तरबृहल्लोकैरन्यं गायत्रयाज्ञियैः ॥
9.m:
The ground must be clearly marked, the peg straight, the measuring cord made of muñja grass and without knottiness; / at the bright moon or beginning [of sacrifices] no defect should be made; the lunar day and asterism should be auspicious to Varuṇa.

All altars are lengthened towards the east; the mould is of the thickness of an axle; / all are equal to half an arva; the height is five knees.

9.s: yajuṣmatīnāṃ saṃkhyā tu sarvāsāṃ caiva niścitā ekaikasyāṃ citau vāpi tāṃ me nigadataḥ śṛṇu ||
9.d: यजुष्मतीनां संख्या तु सर्वासां चैव निश्चिता एकैकस्यां चितौ वापि तां मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
9.m:
In the middle [layer, there is] half of the ṛtavyā bricks, of the nākasad and the pañcacūḍā bricks; / with reference to the mould and other [requisites], the area contains seven and a half [square puruṣas]. (4)

layer by layer, or each individually: listen to it as I declare it.

9.s: ṣaḍaśītiḥ śataṃ tvādyā dvitīyā daśa saptatiḥ trayodaśa tṛtīyā syācchataṃ cāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ caturthī śatamekā syāttisraścaiveṣṭakāḥ smṛtāḥ śatāni trīṇi pañcāśatṣaṭcaiva citiruttamā ||
9.d: षडशीतिः शतं त्वाद्या द्वितीया दश सप्ततिः त्रयोदश तृतीया स्याच्छतं चाहुर्मनीषिणः चतुर्थी शतमेका स्यात्तिस्रश्चैवेष्टकाः स्मृताः शतानि त्रीणि पञ्चाशत्षट्चैव चितिरुत्तमा ॥

9.s: etāḥ sarvā yajuṣmatyo yābhiragniḥ prasūryate śeṣaṃ lokaṃpṛṇābhistu citīnāmabhipūrayet ||
9.d: एताः सर्वा यजुष्मत्यो याभिरग्निः प्रसूर्यते शेषं लोकंपृणाभिस्तु चितीनामभिपूरयेत् ॥
9.m:
All these are yajuṣmatī [bricks], by which the fire[-altar] is generated;

the remainder of the brick layers he should fill up with lokaṃpṛṇā [bricks].

9.s: etāḥ sarvā samāmnātāḥ yajuryāvatpravartate tadetaddhi sahasraṃ syāccharkarābhiḥ sahocyate ||
9.d: एताः सर्वा समाम्नाताः यजुर्यावत्प्रवर्तते तदेतद्धि सहस्रं स्याच्छर्कराभिः सहोच्यते ॥
9.m:
All these are handed down in tradition as far as the Yajus extends;

this amounts to one thousand, spoken of together with the pebbles.

9.s: etā upahitāḥ samyagdhenavastu prajāyante amuṣminyajamānāya kāmānduhyati sarvaśaḥ ||
9.d: एता उपहिताः सम्यग्धेनवस्तु प्रजायन्ते अमुष्मिन्यजमानाय कामान्दुह्यति सर्वशः ॥
9.m:
These, when properly laid, become milch cows;

they milk all desires for that sacrificer in the other world.

9.s: ṣaṣṭiṃ prajāpatiṃ veda yo hi saṃvatsaraḥ smṛtaḥ gacchati brahmaṇo lokaṃ nākaṃ bradhnasya viṣṭapam ||
9.d: षष्टिं प्रजापतिं वेद यो हि संवत्सरः स्मृतः गच्छति ब्रह्मणो लोकं नाकं ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपम् ॥
9.m:
He who knows the sixty[-fold] Prajāpati, who is handed down as the year,

goes to the world of Brahman, to the firmament, the summit of the sun. //9

10.s: vaiṣṇave yā prameyāya śulbavidbhiśca sarvaśaḥ saṃkhyātṛbhyaḥ pravaktṛbhyo namo bharanto yo mase idaṃ bhūmya bhajāmahe yā no mānakṛtāmiva yajñiyaṃ mānamuttamaṃ vardhamānaṃ sve dame ||
10.d: वैष्णवे या प्रमेयाय शुल्बविद्भिश्च सर्वशः संख्यातृभ्यः प्रवक्तृभ्यो नमो भरन्तो यो मसे इदं भूम्य भजामहे या नो मानकृतामिव यज्ञियं मानमुत्तमं वर्धमानं स्वे दमे ॥
10.m:
To the measure that is for Viṣṇu, and by the cord-experts everywhere,

to the enumerators, to the instructors, paying homage, we offer:

[Thinking,] 'Here we distribute the earth, who belongs to us as to measurers,

the supreme sacrificial measure increasing in its own house.'

10.s: spaṣṭā bhūmiṛjuḥ śaṅkurmauñjaṃ śulbamabandhuram citrādau nākṛtiḥ kāryā tithyṛkṣaṃ varuṇaśubham ||
10.d: स्पष्टा भूमिऋजुः शङ्कुर्मौञ्जं शुल्बमबन्धुरम् चित्रादौ नाकृतिः कार्या तिथ्यृक्षं वरुणशुभम् ॥
10.m:
The ground [must be] clear, the peg straight, the measuring cord made of muñja grass and without roughness;

the form should not be constructed during Citrā, etc.; the lunar day and asterism [should be] propitious according to Varuṇa.

10.s: sarvāḥ prāgāyatā vedyaḥ karaṇaṃ yaskadehikam ardhenārvasamaṃ sarvamucchedo jānu pañcakam ||
10.d: सर्वाः प्रागायता वेद्यः करणं यस्कदेहिकम् अर्धेनार्वसमं सर्वमुच्छेदो जानु पञ्चकम् ॥
10.m:
All altars extend toward the east; their construction is by body-measure;

everything is uniform with half [...]; the elevation is five knee[-heights].

In the middle [layer], half of the ṛtavyā [bricks], of the nākasad and the pañcacūḍā [bricks]—

for the sake of the construction and the rest, the area has an interval of seven and a half.

10.s: anaḥsiddhaṃ havirdhānaṃ pātrasiddhāḥ kharāḥ kharāḥ cātvālaḥ paśubhiḥ siddho havirbhiḥ sāgnikāḥ kharāḥ ||
10.d: अनःसिद्धं हविर्धानं पात्रसिद्धाः खराः खराः चात्वालः पशुभिः सिद्धो हविर्भिः साग्निकाः खराः ॥
10.m:
The Havirdhāna shed is established by the carts; the mounds are established by the vessels.

The pit is established by the sacrificial animals; the mounds with the fires are established by the oblations.

10.s: maṇḍalārdhaṃ catuḥsrakti ratnināṃ vihitāḥ kharāḥ aratnirghana eteṣāṃ bhūyastve bhūyasībidhau ||
10.d: मण्डलार्धं चतुःस्रक्ति रत्निनां विहिताः खराः अरत्निर्घन एतेषां भूयस्त्वे भूयसीबिधौ ॥
10.m:
A semicircle, four-cornered, [each] prescribed for cubit-length mounds.

Their depth is one cubit; in case of increase, in the procedure for enlargement.

10.s: pūrvaścaturviṃśatibhāge lekhyaścaturvaṃśairālikhitastu paścimaḥ syāddakṣiṇe 'ṣṭadviguṇena lekhyastriṃśadbhirāyamya haretturāyam ||
10.d: पूर्वश्चतुर्विंशतिभागे लेख्यश्चतुर्वंशैरालिखितस्तु पश्चिमः स्याद्दक्षिणे ऽष्टद्विगुणेन लेख्यस्त्रिंशद्भिरायम्य हरेत्तुरायम् ॥
10.m: The eastern one is to be drawn at the twenty-fourth part; the western one is drawn with four bamboo rods; in the south it is to be drawn with twice eight [parts]; having extended thirty, one should take the transverse.

10.s: udakprakramya cātvālaṃ śāmitraṃ prakrame tataḥ bhūyastatpaśubhūyastve vṛddhiruttarato bhavet ||
10.d: उदक्प्रक्रम्य चात्वालं शामित्रं प्रक्रमे ततः भूयस्तत्पशुभूयस्त्वे वृद्धिरुत्तरतो भवेत् ॥
10.m:
Having stepped one stride north of the pit, then the Śāmitra [shed is situated] at a stride.

Greater than that, in case of an increase of sacrificial animals, the enlargement should be toward the north.

10.s: āyāmabāhuṃ nikṣipya vistarastu tathā pṛthak so 'dhyardhaṃ guṇayedrāśiṃ sa sarvaguṇito ghanaḥ ||
10.d: आयामबाहुं निक्षिप्य विस्तरस्तु तथा पृथक् सो ऽध्यर्धं गुणयेद्राशिं स सर्वगुणितो घनः ॥
10.m:
Having laid out the side of the length, and likewise the breadth separately,

one should multiply that quantity by one and a half; that multiplied by everything is the solid content.

10.s: āyāmamāyāmaguṇaṃ vistāraṃ vistareṇa tu samasya vargamūlaṃ yattatkarṇaṃ tadvido viduḥ ||
10.d: आयाममायामगुणं विस्तारं विस्तरेण तु समस्य वर्गमूलं यत्तत्कर्णं तद्विदो विदुः ॥
10.m:
The length multiplied by the length, and the breadth by the breadth:

the square root of the sum, that is the diagonal—so know those who know it.
Between Śravaṇā and Abhijit, or between Bahulā and Tiṣya, or between Citrā and Svātī, or by fire in water,
at night the sun-track is called the east; on a circle marked by a peg, east and west. //10

11.s: janmanā rogahīno vā yajamāno bhavedyadi kathaṃ tatra pramāṇāni prayoktavyāni kartṛbhiḥ ||
11.d: जन्मना रोगहीनो वा यजमानो भवेद्यदि कथं तत्र प्रमाणानि प्रयोक्तव्यानि कर्तृभिः ॥
11.m:
If the sacrificer should be free from disease from birth,

how then are the measures to be applied there by the builders?

11.s: yadyurutantuḥ keśovāstṛtaḥ sarṣapo yavaścaiva ṣaḍguṇitaḥ ṣaḍguṇito bhavati narasyāṅgulaṃ māne taddvādaśakaṃ prādeśamityāhuḥ ||
11.d: यद्युरुतन्तुः केशोवास्तृतः सर्षपो यवश्चैव षड्गुणितः षड्गुणितो भवति नरस्याङ्गुलं माने तद्द्वादशकं प्रादेशमित्याहुः ॥
11.m: A thigh-hair or hair [laid] flat, a mustard seed, and a barleycorn each multiplied by six becomes a finger-breadth in the measure of a man; twelve of that they call a span.

11.s: taddvayaṃ smṛto 'ratniḥ prakramo 'ratnisamaḥ sa dviḥprādeśo bhaveccitiṣu ||
11.d: तद्द्वयं स्मृतो ऽरत्निः प्रक्रमो ऽरत्निसमः स द्विःप्रादेशो भवेच्चितिषु ॥
11.m: Two of that is traditionally remembered as a cubit; a stride is equal to a cubit; it should be two spans in the brick layers.

11.s: adhyardhāṅgulahīnāścatvāraḥ prakramā bhavenniyatāḥ ||
11.d: अध्यर्धाङ्गुलहीनाश्चत्वारः प्रक्रमा भवेन्नियताः ॥
11.m: Four strides reduced by one and a half finger-breadths should be fixed.

11.s: tatraikādaśa yūpāścatvāraścaturuttarāḥ sattresattre ||
11.d: तत्रैकादश यूपाश्चत्वारश्चतुरुत्तराः सत्त्रेसत्त्रे ॥
11.m: There are eleven sacrificial posts, or four, each increased by four in session after session.

11.s: ekasyāṃ vedyāmagnidvayamiṣṭakāriktaṃ bhavati pṛthagato vediḥ cetpṛthagagniḥ klṛptaḥ ||
11.d: एकस्यां वेद्यामग्निद्वयमिष्टकारिक्तं भवति पृथगतो वेदिः चेत्पृथगग्निः क्लृप्तः ॥
11.m: On a single altar, a pair of fires is without bricks; hence the altar is separate if a separate fire is prepared.

11.s: viṃśatyaṅgulaḥ śataṃ niyataḥ pañcāratnirnaro daśapado vā | hīnātiriktayuktyā dehedehe pramāṇaṃ tu ||
11.d: विंशत्यङ्गुलः शतं नियतः पञ्चारत्निर्नरो दशपदो वा । हीनातिरिक्तयुक्त्या देहेदेहे प्रमाणं तु ॥
11.m: A man is fixed as one hundred and twenty finger-breadths, or five cubits, or ten feet; but in body after body, the measure is by the rule of deficiency and excess.

11.s: ṣaḍaśītiryugamuktaṃ sāṣṭādaśa ucyate tvakṣastantrasamasamastaṃ dvyujaṃ rathamīṣāṃ vyavāsyanti ||
11.d: षडशीतिर्युगमुक्तं साष्टादश उच्यते त्वक्षस्तन्त्रसमसमस्तं द्व्युजं रथमीषां व्यवास्यन्ति ॥
11.m: The yoke is said to be eighty-six [finger-breadths]; the axle is stated as with eighteen; they determine the whole pole-length of a two-horse chariot equal to the warp.

11.s: maṇḍalamatha caturaśraṃ maṇḍalaṃ ca yaḥ kurjāttasyemaṃ karaṇavidhiṃ tadvidāmudāhṛtaṃ śṛṇuta ||
11.d: मण्डलमथ चतुरश्रं मण्डलं च यः कुर्जात्तस्येमं करणविधिं तद्विदामुदाहृतं शृणुत ॥
11.m: Now, one who would make a circle into a square, and a square into a circle: hear this method of execution declared by those who know it!

11.s: maṇḍalaviṣkambhārdhasamastribhujādavalambakaścatuḥsraktiḥ prāgāyatāttribhāgātkarṇāt sa maṇḍalaṃ bhavati ||
11.d: मण्डलविष्कम्भार्धसमस्त्रिभुजादवलम्बकश्चतुःस्रक्तिः प्रागायतात्त्रिभागात्कर्णात् स मण्डलं भवति ॥
11.m: A plumb line from a triangle, equal to half the diameter of the circle, four-cornered, extended east, from one-third of the diagonal: that becomes a circle.

11.s: puruṣaḥ puruṣaṃ kuryāttasyākṣṇayā dvipuruṣaṃ bhaveccaturastasyāpyakṣṇayā dvābhyāṃ vā syāścatuḥpuruṣam ||
11.d: पुरुषः पुरुषं कुर्यात्तस्याक्ष्णया द्विपुरुषं भवेच्चतुरस्तस्याप्यक्ष्णया द्वाभ्यां वा स्याश्चतुःपुरुषम् ॥
11.m: A man-length should make a man-length; along its diagonal it becomes two man-lengths; fourfold, along its diagonal or with two, it would be four man-lengths.

11.s: dvipuruṣaḥ karaṇī śroṇī bāhustu dviguṇo bhavettriṃkuṣṭhavattryavalambakastato yaścaturaśre dvāṣṭamāḥ puruṣāḥ ||
11.d: द्विपुरुषः करणी श्रोणी बाहुस्तु द्विगुणो भवेत्त्रिंकुष्ठवत्त्र्यवलम्बकस्ततो यश्चतुरश्रे द्वाष्टमाः पुरुषाः ॥
11.m: The producing side is two man-lengths; the buttock [side] should be a doubled arm; having three corners, with three plumb lines; then in the square that is two-eighths man-lengths.

11.s: viṣkambhaḥ pañcabhāgaśca viṣkambhastriguṇaśca yaḥ sa maṇḍalaparikṣepo na vālamatiricyate ||
11.d: विष्कम्भः पञ्चभागश्च विष्कम्भस्त्रिगुणश्च यः स मण्डलपरिक्षेपो न वालमतिरिच्यते ॥
11.m:
A diameter and a fifth part, and that which is thrice the diameter:

that is the circumference of a circle; it does not exceed by a hair.

11.s: daśadhā chidya viṣkambhaṃ tribhāgānuddharettataḥ tena yaccaturaśraṃ syānmaṇḍale tadapaprathiḥ ||
11.d: दशधा छिद्य विष्कम्भं त्रिभागानुद्धरेत्ततः तेन यच्चतुरश्रं स्यान्मण्डले तदपप्रथिः ॥
11.m:
Having divided the diameter into ten parts, one should then take away three parts;

that which would be a square with that, is its extension in the circle.

11.s: caturaśraṃ navadhā kuryāddhanuḥkoṭyastridhātridhā utsedhātpañcamaṃ lumpetpurīṣeṇeha tāvatsamaṃ ||
11.d: चतुरश्रं नवधा कुर्याद्धनुःकोट्यस्त्रिधात्रिधा उत्सेधात्पञ्चमं लुम्पेत्पुरीषेणेह तावत्समं ॥
11.m:
One should make a square into nine parts; the tips of the bows in three ways, three ways;

from the height one should remove a fifth part; here it is made so much level with loose earth.

11.s: caturaratnirvā naraḥ sikatākaraṇe tvardhaṃ bhujaḥ pradiśyate ||
11.d: चतुररत्निर्वा नरः सिकताकरणे त्वर्धं भुजः प्रदिश्यते ॥
11.m: Or a man-length is four cubits; but in making with sand, half the arm is assigned.

11.s: karaṇāni tato 'syāḥ kārayettricatuḥpañcatrirabhiparyasya yacchubhaṃ cayaneṣu vidhiḥ purātanairṛṣibhiryo 'bhihitaśca nityaśaḥ ||
11.d: करणानि ततो ऽस्याः कारयेत्त्रिचतुःपञ्चत्रिरभिपर्यस्य यच्छुभं चयनेषु विधिः पुरातनैरृषिभिर्यो ऽभिहितश्च नित्यशः ॥
11.m: Then one should have its constructions made by three, four, and five, turned over thrice—which is an auspicious rule in brick pilings and which has always been declared by the ancient sages.

11.s: parilekhanamānasaṃcayairvyatyāsyaiḥ parimāṇasaṃpadā vedyaḥ sarvāḥ pramāṇairāyāmena ca vistareṇa ca mimīyāt ||
11.d: परिलेखनमानसंचयैर्व्यत्यास्यैः परिमाणसंपदा वेद्यः सर्वाः प्रमाणैरायामेन च विस्तरेण च मिमीयात् ॥
11.m: By delineating, measuring, and heaping, transposed, by excellence of dimension, one should measure all altars with measures, in length and in breadth.

11.s: caturaśrasaṃpadādvyāyāmasamāpanāḥ smṛtā pañcāṅgyātha vā purātanairyāḥ pūrvairṛṣibhiḥ pradarśitāḥ ||
11.d: चतुरश्रसंपदाद्व्यायामसमापनाः स्मृता पञ्चाङ्ग्याथ वा पुरातनैर्याः पूर्वैरृषिभिः प्रदर्शिताः ॥
11.m: Accomplished by the measure of two lengths through excellence of square, or by the cord with five marks, which were shown by the ancient sages of old.

11.s: yaścaiṣa vidhirmaryākṛtastatraiṣā mithunātsamaṃ pañcāṅgī tāvatī rajjuryayā sarvaṃ mimīmahe ṛte kaṅkālajaśyenāṃ steṣāṃ vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam ||
11.d: यश्चैष विधिर्मर्याकृतस्तत्रैषा मिथुनात्समं पञ्चाङ्गी तावती रज्जुर्यया सर्वं मिमीमहे ऋते कङ्कालजश्येनां स्तेषां वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥
11.m: And whatever rule has been established by boundaries, there the cord with five marks is equal to that [derived] from the pair; with that much cord we measure everything, except the eagles born of skeletons; I will declare their characteristic mark.

11.s: iyaṃ mitā yā samayārdhalakṣaṇā tataścaturthe bhavennirāñchanaṃ tato 'rdhaśiṣṭā vistārasamā cayasya | yattataścatuḥkuṣṭhamihānayā caret ||
11.d: इयं मिता या समयार्धलक्षणा ततश्चतुर्थे भवेन्निराञ्छनं ततो ऽर्धशिष्टा विस्तारसमा चयस्य । यत्ततश्चतुःकुष्ठमिहानया चरेत् ॥
11.m: This measured [cord], which has a mark at the middle of the whole; then at the fourth there should be an intermediate mark; then what remains as half is equal to the breadth of the layer; what is four-cornered from that, one should execute with this here.

11.s: prācītathāyāmasamā nidadhyātpāśau nikhanyādatha madhyaṃ ca ||
11.d: प्राचीतथायामसमा निदध्यात्पाशौ निखन्यादथ मध्यं च ॥
11.m: One should lay it facing east, equal to the length; one should fix the two loops and then the middle.

11.s: unmucya paścādatha madhyame tatprāgdakṣiṇāyamya nirāñchanena vistārato 'rdhe nikhaneta śaṅkum | pratyaktathottaramadhyame ca | sa vāsuvedīṣu ||
11.d: उन्मुच्य पश्चादथ मध्यमे तत्प्राग्दक्षिणायम्य निराञ्छनेन विस्तारतो ऽर्धे निखनेत शङ्कुम् । प्रत्यक्तथोत्तरमध्यमे च । स वासुवेदीषु ॥
11.m: Then having released from the west, stretching it toward the east and south from the middle, one should drive a peg at half the breadth by means of the intermediate mark; likewise toward the west and in the northern middle; that is on the ground-altars.

11.s: atha mānametacchroṇyāṃ tu pāśoddharaṇaṃ kriyeta ||
11.d: अथ मानमेतच्छ्रोण्यां तु पाशोद्धरणं क्रियेत ॥
11.m: Now this measure: the lifting of the loops should be made at the buttock.

11.s: aṃsaśroṇyorlikhet dikṣu lekhāḥ | śaṅkū nihanyātsamareṣu teṣu | tebhyaḥ samantātparilekhayet ||
11.d: अंसश्रोण्योर्लिखेत् दिक्षु लेखाः । शङ्कू निहन्यात्समरेषु तेषु । तेभ्यः समन्तात्परिलेखयेत् ॥
11.m: At the shoulders and buttocks one should draw lines in the cardinal directions; one should drive pegs at those intersections; from them one should delineate all around.

11.s: yadyaiṣṭikā nobhau likheta śiṣṭau ||
11.d: यद्यैष्टिका नोभौ लिखेत शिष्टौ ॥
11.m: If it is made of bricks, one should not draw the two remaining [lines].

11.s: pūrve tribhāge tvapare ca siddhopasthitāvutkaradakṣiṇāgnī ||
11.d: पूर्वे त्रिभागे त्वपरे च सिद्धोपस्थितावुत्करदक्षिणाग्नी ॥
11.m: In the eastern third and in the western third, the rubbish heap and the Dakṣiṇāgni fire are established and placed.

11.s: athānyadasya parilekhanaṃ tu madhye bhaveddikṣu navāṅguleneti ||
11.d: अथान्यदस्य परिलेखनं तु मध्ये भवेद्दिक्षु नवाङ्गुलेनेति ॥
11.m: Now another delineation of it should be at the middle, nine finger-breadths in the cardinal directions. //11

12.s: pramāṇārdhaṃ tu ṣaṣṭayūnaṃ viśeṣa iti saṅjñitam viśeṣaśca pramāṇaṃ ca pramāṇasyākṣṇayā bhavet ||
12.d: प्रमाणार्धं तु षष्टयूनं विशेष इति सङ्ज्ञितम् विशेषश्च प्रमाणं च प्रमाणस्याक्ष्णया भवेत् ॥
12.m:
Half a measure reduced by a sixtieth is known as the excess;

and the excess and the measure together become the diagonal of the measure.

12.s: pramāṇārdhamanyatsyāt pāśaṣaṣṭhe sacaturviṃśe lakṣaṇaṃ karoti tannirāñchanamakṣṇayā tiryaṅmānī śeṣaḥ pāśādardhaśaye śroṇī dva ||
12.d: प्रमाणार्धमन्यत्स्यात् पाशषष्ठे सचतुर्विंशे लक्षणं करोति तन्निराञ्छनमक्ष्णया तिर्यङ्मानी शेषः पाशादर्धशये श्रोणी द्व ॥
12.m: There should be another half-measure; at one-sixth of the loop, at twenty-four, one makes a mark; that intermediate mark along the diagonal is the transverse measure; the remainder from the loop is the buttock on half the resting place […].
[…] and the Āgnīdhra shed is instructed here.

12.s: agneryadakṣṇayāmānaṃ tasya caiva tadakṣṇayā tadāśvamedhikaṃ vidyādekaviṃśadvidhau 'thavā ||
12.d: अग्नेर्यदक्ष्णयामानं तस्य चैव तदक्ष्णया तदाश्वमेधिकं विद्यादेकविंशद्विधौ ऽथवा ॥
12.m:
Whatever is the diagonal measure of the fire, and along that [fire's] diagonal,

one should know that as pertaining to the horse sacrifice, or in the twenty-one-fold rite.

12.s: puruṣastiryagbhavedyadanudaśadhā yo mitaḥ tasya karṇena yatkṣetraṃ vidyādekādaśaṃ tu tat ||
12.d: पुरुषस्तिर्यग्भवेद्यदनुदशधा यो मितः तस्य कर्णेन यत्क्षेत्रं विद्यादेकादशं तु तत् ॥
12.m:
The man-length should be transverse; what is measured tenfold,

the area formed by its diagonal one should know as the eleventh [man-length].

12.s: ubhau bāhū naśakṣṇāṃ tu narastiryaktadakṣṇayā ekoccatānaikaśatādbāhuvṛddhayā vivardhayet ||
12.d: उभौ बाहू नशक्ष्णां तु नरस्तिर्यक्तदक्ष्णया एकोच्चतानैकशताद्बाहुवृद्धया विवर्धयेत् ॥
12.m:
Both arms […]; the man-length is transverse; along its diagonal,

one should increase from one elevated hundred and one by an increase of the arms. //12

13.s: avalambakakuṣṭhe tu yo bhavetṣoḍaśāṅgule sautrāmaṇyā bhavedeṣa prakramo mānakarmaṇi ||
13.d: अवलम्बककुष्ठे तु यो भवेत्षोडशाङ्गुले सौत्रामण्या भवेदेष प्रक्रमो मानकर्मणि ॥
13.m:
The side of the plumb line which is sixteen finger-breadths,

this should be the stride of the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice in the work of measuring.

13.s: prakramasya tṛtīyena saumikī sārparājñikī saṃtṛtīyaistribhiścānyaiḥ siddhamauttaravedikam ||
13.d: प्रक्रमस्य तृतीयेन सौमिकी सार्पराज्ञिकी संतृतीयैस्त्रिभिश्चान्यैः सिद्धमौत्तरवेदिकम् ॥
13.m:
With a third of a stride [is measured] the Soma [altar] and the Sārparājñī [altar];

and with three other thirds, the high altar is established.

13.s: caturdaśāṅgulo vā syātprakramastena saumikī śatairdvādaśabhirvāpi minuyātpāśukāmiva ||
13.d: चतुर्दशाङ्गुलो वा स्यात्प्रक्रमस्तेन सौमिकी शतैर्द्वादशभिर्वापि मिनुयात्पाशुकामिव ॥
13.m:
Or the stride may be fourteen finger-breadths; by that the Soma [altar] is measured.

Or he should measure [it] with twelve hundreds, like that for the animal sacrifice. \3\

13.s: sacaturthe vanaṃ ṣaḍbhirnavabhirvātha saptabhiḥ navabhirvāparaṃ cakraṃ karaṇādhe na lekhayet ||
13.d: सचतुर्थे वनं षड्भिर्नवभिर्वाथ सप्तभिः नवभिर्वापरं चक्रं करणाधे न लेखयेत् ॥
13.m:
With a fourth [added], the grove [is measured] by six, or nine, or seven,

or the next wheel by nine; he should not draw [it] on half the producing side. \4\

13.s: caturṣu nivapedeṣāṃ sāvitrādiṣu yo vidhiḥ aruṇe jānudaghne nikhanyādadbhistu pūrayet ||
13.d: चतुर्षु निवपेदेषां सावित्रादिषु यो विधिः अरुणे जानुदघ्ने निखन्यादद्भिस्तु पूरयेत् ॥
13.m:
In the four he should cast down the rule which [applies] to the Sāvitra and the others;

at the Aruṇa [altar] he should dig knee-deep and fill [it] with water. \5\

13.s: caturaśramathāpi maṇḍalaṃ dvividhaṃ gārhapatyalakṣaṇaṃ vyāyāmamitaṃ caturbhujaṃ puruṣārdhena tu maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet ||
13.d: चतुरश्रमथापि मण्डलं द्विविधं गार्हपत्यलक्षणं व्यायाममितं चतुर्भुजं पुरुषार्धेन तु मण्डलं परिलिखेत् ॥
13.m: Now, the square or circular characteristic of the Gārhapatya is twofold: a four-sided [square] measured by a fathom, but he should circumscribe the circle with half a man-length. \6\

13.s: vyāyāmatṛtīyamāyāntaṃ caturaśraṃ saptamabhāgavistṛtaṃ prāgācitamuttarācitaṃ vyatyāse tadathaikaviṃśakam ||
13.d: व्यायामतृतीयमायान्तं चतुरश्रं सप्तमभागविस्तृतं प्रागाचितमुत्तराचितं व्यत्यासे तदथैकविंशकम् ॥
13.m: A square having the length of a third of a fathom and the breadth of a seventh part; piled toward the east and piled toward the north alternately; that [altar] consists of twenty-one [bricks]. \7\

13.s: puruṣasya tṛtīyamāyāntaṃ caturaśraṃ ṣaḍbhāgavistṛtam | prathikaśca tadāyato bhavenmadhye tena samāyato bhavenmadhye tena samāstike śeṣau | koṇau prathikamitau samau tadvistārakṛtau viśākhaḥ ||
13.d: पुरुषस्य तृतीयमायान्तं चतुरश्रं षड्भागविस्तृतम् । प्रथिकश्च तदायतो भवेन्मध्ये तेन समायतो भवेन्मध्ये तेन समास्तिके शेषौ । कोणौ प्रथिकमितौ समौ तद्विस्तारकृतौ विशाखः ॥
13.m: A square having the length of a third of a man-length and the breadth of a sixth part; and let the wide [brick] be long; in the middle, equal in length to it; in the middle, equal to it in laying; the remaining two corners are measured like the wide one, equal, made to its breadth; [it is] branching. \8\

13.s: ṣaḍbhāgakṛtāyāmo bhaveddvyardhe tu trikoṇasaṃsthite ||
13.d: षड्भागकृतायामो भवेद्द्व्यर्धे तु त्रिकोणसंस्थिते ॥
13.m: Let its length be made of a sixth part; but in the two and a half [parts] it stands triangular. \9\

13.s: caturaśravipāṇakaḥ prathiko 'rdhaṃ prathikaśca yo mitaḥ ||
13.d: चतुरश्रविपाणकः प्रथिको ऽर्धं प्रथिकश्च यो मितः ॥
13.m: The square-viṣāṇaka, the wide one, and the half-wide one which is measured. \10\

13.s: karaṇāni bhavanti maṇḍale catvāri pramitāni bhāgaśaḥ ||
13.d: करणानि भवन्ति मण्डले चत्वारि प्रमितानि भागशः ॥
13.m: There are four producing sides in the circle, measured part by part. \11\

13.s: madhye 'sya catasra iṣṭakāḥ tatpūrvāparayordvayordvayam | prathiko 'rdha viṣāṇikadvayaṃ punareva punaraiti maṇḍalamardhaprathikadvaye samaṃ saṃpūrṇam | tadathaikaviṃśakam ||
13.d: मध्ये ऽस्य चतस्र इष्टकाः तत्पूर्वापरयोर्द्वयोर्द्वयम् । प्रथिको ऽर्ध विषाणिकद्वयं पुनरेव पुनरैति मण्डलमर्धप्रथिकद्वये समं संपूर्णम् । तदथैकविंशकम् ॥
13.m: In the middle of this are four bricks, two on each of its east and west sides; two wide ones, half [a wide one], two horn-shaped [bricks]; again indeed the circle is reached; complete, equal to two half-wide ones; that [altar] consists of twenty-one [bricks]. \12\

13.s: vyatyāsamudaṅmukhena saha vyatyasyedvetyuttarottaram ||
13.d: व्यत्यासमुदङ्मुखेन सह व्यत्यस्येद्वेत्युत्तरोत्तरम् ॥
13.m: He should alternate [the layers], alternating with one facing north, sequentially layer by layer. \13\

13.s: adhyardhaṃ padyaṃ ca padyārdhapadyapādavatpadyārdhotsedhamityāhurgāyatre karaṇāni ca ||
13.d: अध्यर्धं पद्यं च पद्यार्धपद्यपादवत्पद्यार्धोत्सेधमित्याहुर्गायत्रे करणानि च ॥
13.m: One and a half, a foot-brick, and having a half-foot and a quarter-foot, with a height of half a foot—these are said to be the producing sides for the Gāyatra [altar]. \14\

13.s: caturguṇāṃ dvipuruṣāṃ rajjuṃ kṛtvā samāhitām || saṃbhāgajñātṛtodāntāṃ pañcāṅgīṃ tadvido viduḥ ||
13.d: चतुर्गुणां द्विपुरुषां रज्जुं कृत्वा समाहिताम् ॥ संभागज्ञातृतोदान्तां पञ्चाङ्गीं तद्विदो विदुः ॥
13.m:
Having made an orderly cord of fourfold [thickness] and two man-lengths,

ending at the pointers known to the parts, those who know it know [it as] the cord with five marks. \15\

13.s: madhyamātpāśayostodo gāyatramānamucyate | sāratnāvardhapuruṣe | caturaśrastayā mitaḥ | pakṣapucchāntayorvṛddhyā gāyatreṇetareṣubhiḥ ||
13.d: मध्यमात्पाशयोस्तोदो गायत्रमानमुच्यते । सारत्नावर्धपुरुषे । चतुरश्रस्तया मितः । पक्षपुच्छान्तयोर्वृद्ध्या गायत्रेणेतरेषुभिः ॥
13.m: From the middle to the loops, the pointer is called the Gāyatra measure; [measured] at half a man-length with a cubit, the square is measured by it; with the expansion of the two wing ends and tail, [it is measured] by the Gāyatra [and] by the other arrows. \16\

13.s: iṣṭakā śoṣapākābhyāṃ triṃśanmānāttu hīyate ||
13.d: इष्टका शोषपाकाभ्यां त्रिंशन्मानात्तु हीयते ॥
13.m: Through drying and baking, the brick is reduced from the thirty-measure. \17\

13.s: tataḥ kṣetraṃ tricaturbhāgaṃ niruhyādāpayecchivam ||
13.d: ततः क्षेत्रं त्रिचतुर्भागं निरुह्यादापयेच्छिवम् ॥
13.m: Then, having shifted out three-fourths of the area, he should offer propitiation. \18\

13.s: aṃsa uttareṃ 'se ca prācyo 'dhyardhāstu viṃśatirdaśa pucche dvirdvādaśakau pakṣayorabhitaḥ pucche tu pañca deyāḥ pañca prācīḥ pañcadaśa dadyācchirasi | caturaśītī pakṣayoḥ pañcāśataṃ triṃśatamātmani padyā bhavanti śatamekonaṃ puccheṃ 'saśroṇyorviṃśatirviṃśatiḥ pucche pakṣayordaśadaśāhuḥ ||
13.d: अंस उत्तरें ऽसे च प्राच्यो ऽध्यर्धास्तु विंशतिर्दश पुच्छे द्विर्द्वादशकौ पक्षयोरभितः पुच्छे तु पञ्च देयाः पञ्च प्राचीः पञ्चदश दद्याच्छिरसि । चतुरशीती पक्षयोः पञ्चाशतं त्रिंशतमात्मनि पद्या भवन्ति शतमेकोनं पुच्छें ऽसश्रोण्योर्विंशतिर्विंशतिः पुच्छे पक्षयोर्दशदशाहुः ॥
13.m: At the shoulder and on the northern shoulder, twenty [bricks of] one-and-a-half facing east; ten on the tail; twice twelve on the two wings; on both sides on the tail, five should be placed; he should place five facing east; fifteen on the head; eighty-four on the wings; fifty on the body; thirty foot-bricks; on the tail ninety-nine; twenty each on the shoulder and buttock; on the tail and two wings they say ten each. \19\

13.s: adhyardhā daśa śirasi prācyudīcyo bhavanti ||
13.d: अध्यर्धा दश शिरसि प्राच्युदीच्यो भवन्ति ॥
13.m: Ten [bricks of] one-and-a-half on the head facing east and north. \20\

13.s: pūrvopahitā prathamā padayujaḥ sarvā | dvitīyāvāgyujo 'śvinī ||
13.d: पूर्वोपहिता प्रथमा पदयुजः सर्वा । द्वितीयावाग्युजो ऽश्विनी ॥
13.m: All the first [layer] placed earlier are foot-coupled; the second are speech-coupled and Aśvin-coupled. \21\

13.s: vyatyāsaṃ cinuyādevaṃ jānunāsya vartmasu ||
13.d: व्यत्यासं चिनुयादेवं जानुनास्य वर्त्मसु ॥
13.m: In this way he should pile alternately, with the knee on its tracks. \22\

13.s: tripadā alpakṣetrā ekacitikāścatuḥ karaṇayuktāḥ dhiṣṇyā bhavanti sāgnicityamantrāḥ sātiriktāśca ||
13.d: त्रिपदा अल्पक्षेत्रा एकचितिकाश्चतुः करणयुक्ताः धिष्ण्या भवन्ति साग्निचित्यमन्त्राः सातिरिक्ताश्च ॥
13.m: The dhiṣṇya hearths are three feet [wide], of small area, having a single brick layer, provided with four producing sides, accompanied by mantras for piling the fire, and with additional [bricks]. \23\

13.s: adhyardhāstu catasro dve madhye nakaulaścaturbhāgaḥ ||
13.d: अध्यर्धास्तु चतस्रो द्वे मध्ये नकौलश्चतुर्भागः ॥
13.m: Four [bricks of] one-and-a-half, two in the middle, an ichneumon-shaped one, [and] a quarter [brick]. \24\

13.s: aśmā navamo 'gnīdhre ||
13.d: अश्मा नवमो ऽग्नीध्रे ॥

13.s: hotrīyamataḥ saṃvakṣyāmo | aṃsaśroṇyoḥ padyāśrayā nakulakā bahistisṛṣu dikṣvantaścaturdaśa padakacaturthāḥ sa yaḥ pratidiśamaṣṭau padyā dikṣu vidikṣu ||
13.d: होत्रीयमतः संवक्ष्यामो । अंसश्रोण्योः पद्याश्रया नकुलका बहिस्तिसृषु दिक्ष्वन्तश्चतुर्दश पदकचतुर्थाः स यः प्रतिदिशमष्टौ पद्या दिक्षु विदिक्षु ॥
13.m: Now we shall explain the Hotṛ's hearth: supported on foot-bricks at the shoulder and buttock, ichneumon-shaped outside in the three directions, inside fourteen quarter foot-bricks; that which has eight foot-bricks in each direction, in the cardinal directions and intermediate directions. \26\

13.s: brāhmaṇācchaṃsye daśa caikā syurmadhye dvau dvau caturthyau nakulaśca ||
13.d: ब्राह्मणाच्छंस्ये दश चैका स्युर्मध्ये द्वौ द्वौ चतुर्थ्यौ नकुलश्च ॥
13.m: In the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's hearth there should be eleven; in the middle two each of fourths, and an ichneumon-shaped one. \27\

13.s: abhitastisraḥ padyā dve madhye 'dhyardhe śiṣṭeṣvaṣṭau ||
13.d: अभितस्तिस्रः पद्या द्वे मध्ये ऽध्यर्धे शिष्टेष्वष्टौ ॥
13.m: On both sides three foot-bricks, two in the middle, in the remaining [hearths] eight one-and-a-half bricks. \28\

13.s: adhyardhāḥ ṣaṇmārjālīyeṃ 'sa mārjālīyaṃ syāddakṣiṇapārśvena śāmitraṃ cātvālasya ca paścād vabhṛthakalpe 'pyevaṃ padamekatastripadastisro 'tirikteṣviti ||
13.d: अध्यर्धाः षण्मार्जालीयें ऽस मार्जालीयं स्याद्दक्षिणपार्श्वेन शामित्रं चात्वालस्य च पश्चाद् वभृथकल्पे ऽप्येवं पदमेकतस्त्रिपदस्तिस्रो ऽतिरिक्तेष्विति ॥
13.m: Six [bricks of] one-and-a-half in the Mārjālīya; the Mārjālīya should be at the shoulder; on the southern side, the Śāmitra [shed]; and behind the pit; also in the rite of the final bath, thus: one foot on one side, three feet, three in the extra ones. \29\ \\13\\

14.s: saptatriṃśatsārdhāḥ pakṣaḥ savyaśca śirasi catvāraḥ ṣaḍviṃśakastathātma śyene pañcadaśakaṃ puccham | saptadaśakaṃ pucchaṃ dvayaṃ śirasyātmapakṣayoḥ klṛptamalajasya | bhāgasaṃdhāntayajñaiḥ pramitānnaracaturthe ||
14.d: सप्तत्रिंशत्सार्धाः पक्षः सव्यश्च शिरसि चत्वारः षड्विंशकस्तथात्म श्येने पञ्चदशकं पुच्छम् । सप्तदशकं पुच्छं द्वयं शिरस्यात्मपक्षयोः क्लृप्तमलजस्य । भागसंधान्तयज्ञैः प्रमितान्नरचतुर्थे ॥
14.m: Thirty-seven and a half [is] the left wing, and four on the head; twenty-six likewise the body; in the falcon [altar] fifteen is the tail; seventeen is the tail, two on the head, prepared on the body and wings of the alaja bird; measured by the rites of joining the parts, in a fourth of a man-length. \1\

14.s: aṣṭau bhāgāḥ pucchaṃ kaṅkacite bhavanti pādayoścaturaḥ śirasi tu sapta jñeyāḥ śyenavadātmā ca pakṣau ca ||
14.d: अष्टौ भागाः पुच्छं कङ्कचिते भवन्ति पादयोश्चतुरः शिरसि तु सप्त ज्ञेयाः श्येनवदात्मा च पक्षौ च ॥
14.m: Eight parts are the tail in the heron piling; four on the feet; seven should be known on the head; the body and wings are like the falcon. \2\

14.s: śyenālajakaṅkānāmaṣṭau sārdhā vistṛtaṃ pucchaṃ catvārotmā dvau ca śiraḥ sarveṣāṃ pañcakau pakṣau ||
14.d: श्येनालजकङ्कानामष्टौ सार्धा विस्तृतं पुच्छं चत्वारोत्मा द्वौ च शिरः सर्वेषां पञ्चकौ पक्षौ ॥
14.m: Of the falcon, the alaja, and the heron, the tail is eight and a half in width, the body four, and the head two; of all, the wings are five each. \3\

14.s: śyenālajakaṅkānāṃ dvitricatuḥ kuṣṭhamityucyate puccham | pañcākṣṇāḥ pakṣapātrāstvakṣṇābhiḥ pariśritāḥ ||
14.d: श्येनालजकङ्कानां द्वित्रिचतुः कुष्ठमित्युच्यते पुच्छम् । पञ्चाक्ष्णाः पक्षपात्रास्त्वक्ष्णाभिः परिश्रिताः ॥
14.m: Of the falcon, the alaja, and the heron, the tail is called two-, three-, and four-jointed; five diagonals are the wing-vessels, enclosed by diagonals. \4\

14.s: pucche dvau bhāgāvānayetpucchamalajena trikuṣṭhavattrīnśyenapucchācchirasi kaṅke pādau tu haret ||
14.d: पुच्छे द्वौ भागावानयेत्पुच्छमलजेन त्रिकुष्ठवत्त्रीन्श्येनपुच्छाच्छिरसि कङ्के पादौ तु हरेत् ॥
14.m: He should bring two parts to the tail; the tail like the three-jointed with the alaja; he should take away two feet from the falcon's tail to the head in the heron. \5\

14.s: prācīrdvādaśa sārdhā viṃśatirudīcīrbhavenmitā bhāgā | daśa pañca kaṅkacitāvalaja udīcīstrayodaśa sārdhāśca ||
14.d: प्राचीर्द्वादश सार्धा विंशतिरुदीचीर्भवेन्मिता भागा । दश पञ्च कङ्कचितावलज उदीचीस्त्रयोदश सार्धाश्च ॥
14.m: Twelve and a half parts facing east; twenty parts measured facing north; fifteen in the heron piling; and thirteen and a half facing north in the alaja. \6\

14.s: tricaturbhāgamānī syādrajjurardhatrayodaśī madhye ca lakṣaṇaṃ tasyāścaturbhāgairnirāñchanam ||
14.d: त्रिचतुर्भागमानी स्याद्रज्जुरर्धत्रयोदशी मध्ये च लक्षणं तस्याश्चतुर्भागैर्निराञ्छनम् ॥
14.m:
The cord measuring three-fourths should be twelve and a half [parts long];

and the mark in its middle is the intermediate mark by four parts. \7\

14.s: bhāgikāścatvārastodā ardhaṣaṣṭhe 'paraḥ smṛtaḥ ardhāśca me 'ṣṭame caiva navame daśame 'paraḥ ardhadvādaśo vānyaḥ ||
14.d: भागिकाश्चत्वारस्तोदा अर्धषष्ठे ऽपरः स्मृतः अर्धाश्च मे ऽष्टमे चैव नवमे दशमे ऽपरः अर्धद्वादशो वान्यः ॥
14.m:
Four pointers belonging to the parts; another is recorded at the five-and-a-half;

and at half my eighth, and at the ninth, [and] another at the tenth;

14.s: tataḥ prācīḥ prasārya tu tasyā nikhānayecchaṅkum | pāśayormadhyame 'ṣṭame | caturthe vāhatya pāśam | āsajya madhyame nirāñchanam ||
14.d: ततः प्राचीः प्रसार्य तु तस्या निखानयेच्छङ्कुम् । पाशयोर्मध्यमे ऽष्टमे । चतुर्थे वाहत्य पाशम् । आसज्य मध्यमे निराञ्छनम् ॥
14.m: Then, having stretched [it] facing east, he should drive a peg for it; having fastened the loop at the middle of the two loops, at the eighth or at the fourth, having attached the intermediate mark at the middle. \9\

14.s: nirāyamya vinudyonmucya madhyamāt | abhito daśama āyamya bhāgā dvikacatuṣkāḥ | ardhaṣaṣṭhe 'pi cāhatya pūrvādevaṃ samācaret | tulyaṃ śaṅkuṃ turye ||
14.d: निरायम्य विनुद्योन्मुच्य मध्यमात् । अभितो दशम आयम्य भागा द्विकचतुष्काः । अर्धषष्ठे ऽपि चाहत्य पूर्वादेवं समाचरेत् । तुल्यं शङ्कुं तुर्ये ॥
14.m: Having stretched out, having pushed off, having unfastened from the middle; having stretched on both sides at the tenth, the parts are pairs and fours; and having driven [a peg] at the five-and-a-half, he should proceed thus from the east; an equal peg at the fourth. \10\

14.s: tataḥ prācīḥ prasārya tu ardhaṣaṣṭhakayoḥ pāśau | śaṅkū ardhāṣṭame 'ṣṭame | pragṛhya paścimaśaṅkū | dvikayorvotsṛjettataḥ ||
14.d: ततः प्राचीः प्रसार्य तु अर्धषष्ठकयोः पाशौ । शङ्कू अर्धाष्टमे ऽष्टमे । प्रगृह्य पश्चिमशङ्कू । द्विकयोर्वोत्सृजेत्ततः ॥
14.m: Then, having stretched facing east, the two loops at the two five-and-a-half marks, the two pegs at the seven-and-a-half and the eighth; having grasped the two western pegs, he should release then at the two two-marks. \11\

14.s: caturthanavamau śaṅkū pravṛhedantimāvubhau ||
14.d: चतुर्थनवमौ शङ्कू प्रवृहेदन्तिमावुभौ ॥
14.m: He should pull out both end pegs, the fourth and the ninth. \12\

14.s: aṣṭame pāśamāsṛjya aṣṭamenaiva nigrahaḥ | bhāgebhāge tataḥ śaṅkū tayoḥ ||
14.d: अष्टमे पाशमासृज्य अष्टमेनैव निग्रहः । भागेभागे ततः शङ्कू तयोः ॥
14.m: Having cast the loop at the eighth, the hold is made by the eighth itself; then at every part the two pegs of those two. \13\

14.s: aṣṭame pāśamāsṛjya ādiśaṅkau nigṛhya ca daśame śaṅkumāhanyātpucchārdhe alajasya tu ||
14.d: अष्टमे पाशमासृज्य आदिशङ्कौ निगृह्य च दशमे शङ्कुमाहन्यात्पुच्छार्धे अलजस्य तु ॥
14.m:
Having cast the loop at the eighth, and having held at the first peg,

he should drive a peg at the tenth, at half the tail of the alaja. \14\

14.s: syārdhāṣṭame śaṅkuḥ kaṅkasya darśane smṛtaḥ ||
14.d: स्यार्धाष्टमे शङ्कुः कङ्कस्य दर्शने स्मृतः ॥
14.m: At the seven-and-a-half a peg is recorded in the observation of the heron. \15\

14.s: trike pāśaṃ samāsṛjya daśakena nigṛhya ca etābhyāmeva todābhyāṃ śaṅkū deyau tathottarau ||
14.d: त्रिके पाशं समासृज्य दशकेन निगृह्य च एताभ्यामेव तोदाभ्यां शङ्कू देयौ तथोत्तरौ ॥
14.m:
Having attached the loop at the three, and having held with the ten,

by these two pointers two northern pegs should likewise be placed. \16\

14.s: ardhadvādaśame pāśastriko nigrahaṇo bhavet ādipāśe dvike caiva śaṅkū deyau tathottarau ||
14.d: अर्धद्वादशमे पाशस्त्रिको निग्रहणो भवेत् आदिपाशे द्विके चैव शङ्कू देयौ तथोत्तरौ ॥
14.m:
At the eleven-and-a-half is the loop; the three should be the holding [point];

at the first loop and at the two, two northern pegs should likewise be placed. \17\

14.s: uttare dvikamāsajya dakṣiṇaṃ samayorharet ||
14.d: उत्तरे द्विकमासज्य दक्षिणं समयोर्हरेत् ॥
14.m: Having attached the two on the north, he should take the south at the two equals. \18\

14.s: caturthe śaṅkumāhanyādviparītaṃ samācaret caturthe tu tadarthena nirgṛhya ca ||
14.d: चतुर्थे शङ्कुमाहन्याद्विपरीतं समाचरेत् चतुर्थे तु तदर्थेन निर्गृह्य च ॥
14.m:
He should drive a peg at the fourth; he should do the reverse;

but at the fourth, having grasped with its half, […] \19\

14.s: iti śyenasya rajjurdvādaśalakṣaṇā ||
14.d: इति श्येनस्य रज्जुर्द्वादशलक्षणा ॥
14.m: Such is the measuring cord of twelve marks for the falcon [altar]. \20\

14.s: catvāri karaṇānyeṣāṃ tricaturthena kārayet navabhāgā akṣṇārdhākṣṇāḥ pañcakoṇāḥ ca bhāgaśaḥ ||
14.d: चत्वारि करणान्येषां त्रिचतुर्थेन कारयेत् नवभागा अक्ष्णार्धाक्ष्णाः पञ्चकोणाः च भागशः ॥
14.m:
One should make four producing sizes of these by means of three-fourths [parts]:

Nine-part [bricks], diagonal [half-bricks], half-diagonal [quarter-bricks], and five-cornered [bricks], according to their parts. \21\

14.s: prācīne pañcakoṇe dve athārdhākṣṇādvayaṃ nyaset aṃsāgrayorathaikaikā evaṃ pakṣavipakṣayoḥ ||
14.d: प्राचीने पञ्चकोणे द्वे अथार्धाक्ष्णाद्वयं न्यसेत् अंसाग्रयोरथैकैका एवं पक्षविपक्षयोः ॥
14.m:
One should place two five-cornered [bricks] facing east, and then a pair of half-diagonals;

Then one each at the two shoulder-tips; in the same way on the two wings. \22\

14.s: navabhāgaiścitaṃ madhyamakṣṇābhiḥ pariṣiñcate pakṣāgre pañca patrāṇyevaṃ cākṣṇā vidhīyate ||
14.d: नवभागैश्चितं मध्यमक्ष्णाभिः परिषिञ्चते पक्षाग्रे पञ्च पत्राण्येवं चाक्ष्णा विधीयते ॥
14.m:
The middle [body] is piled with nine-part [bricks]; it is enclosed with diagonals;

At the wing-tip are five feathers; and in this manner the diagonal [brick] is prescribed. \23\

14.s: vyatyāsākṣṇādvayaṃ tunde pañcakoṇe pratyaksthite ardhākṣṇe kaṇṭhasaṃdhyośca pūrayedamitaṃ śiraḥ ||
14.d: व्यत्यासाक्ष्णाद्वयं तुन्दे पञ्चकोणे प्रत्यक्स्थिते अर्धाक्ष्णे कण्ठसंध्योश्च पूरयेदमितं शिरः ॥
14.m:
Two alternating diagonal [bricks] on the belly; two five-cornered [bricks] situated to the west;

And two half-diagonals at the joints of the neck; one should fill out the unmeasured head. \24\

14.s: dve pakṣasaṃdhyorardhākṣṇe pucchasaṃdhyostathāpare daśa pañca ca pucchāgre pakṣāgra ekaviṃśatim ||
14.d: द्वे पक्षसंध्योरर्धाक्ष्णे पुच्छसंध्योस्तथापरे दश पञ्च च पुच्छाग्रे पक्षाग्र एकविंशतिम् ॥
14.m:
Two half-diagonals at the two wing-joints, and similarly two others at the tail-joints;

Ten and five at the tip of the tail, and twenty-one at the wing-tip. \25\

14.s: aupamāne cayane caiṣāṃ vyatyāse karaṇeṣu ca rajjvāścāvapanaṃ hrāso śyenasiddhiriti sthitiḥ ||
14.d: औपमाने चयने चैषां व्यत्यासे करणेषु च रज्ज्वाश्चावपनं ह्रासो श्येनसिद्धिरिति स्थितिः ॥
14.m:
In the model piling of these, and in the alternation, and in the producing sides,

The insertion and shortening of the cord is the established rule for accomplishing the falcon [altar]. \26\

14.s: avakrapakṣamalajaṃ ca pūrvapakṣe tathāyutam madhyāt prasiddhaṃ pucchaṃ śyene dāmnā prasidhyata iti ||
14.d: अवक्रपक्षमलजं च पूर्वपक्षे तथायुतम् मध्यात् प्रसिद्धं पुच्छं श्येने दाम्ना प्रसिध्यत इति ॥
14.m:
The straight-winged [falcon] and the Alaja [altar] are likewise joined in the previous section;

From the center the tail is known; in the case of the falcon, it is accomplished by the cord. \27\

14.s: navamātprāgbhāge śaṅkū turīyasya karaṇam alaje pakṣārdhamavakratāddhyevaṃ bhavet ||
14.d: नवमात्प्राग्भागे शङ्कू तुरीयस्य करणम् अलजे पक्षार्धमवक्रताद्ध्येवं भवेत् ॥
14.m:
East of the ninth [part], two pegs; [this is] the producing side of the fourth [part].

In the Alaja, half of the wing would thus indeed be from straightness. \28\ \\14\\

15.s: puruṣasya tṛtīyapañcamau bhāgau tatkaraṇaṃ punaściteḥ tasyārdhamathāparaṃ bhavettricitikamagnicitiścet ||
15.d: पुरुषस्य तृतीयपञ्चमौ भागौ तत्करणं पुनश्चितेः तस्यार्धमथापरं भवेत्त्रिचितिकमग्निचितिश्चेत् ॥
15.m:
The third and fifth parts of a man-length: that is the producing size for the piling again.

Half of that would be another; if the fire-piling is of three brick layers, \1\

15.s: aṣṭāvaṣṭau raṃmitā citiraṣṭaikādaśikā ca madhyamā vyatyāsavatīrupanya sedaṣṭau dvādaśa cottamā citiḥ ||
15.d: अष्टावष्टौ रंमिता चितिरष्टैकादशिका च मध्यमा व्यत्यासवतीरुपन्य सेदष्टौ द्वादश चोत्तमा चितिः ॥
15.m:
Eight [parts] by eight is measured for the [first] brick layer, and eight by eleven for the middle one;

One should lay down [bricks] having alternations; eight by twelve is the topmost brick layer. \2\

15.s: pañcadaśanaraṃ kṣetraṃ praugacittatastvardham madhyāddaśake trikuṣṭhametattathā karaṇam ||
15.d: पञ्चदशनरं क्षेत्रं प्रौगचित्ततस्त्वर्धम् मध्याद्दशके त्रिकुष्ठमेतत्तथा करणम् ॥
15.m:
The area is fifteen man-lengths; but for the Prauga altar it is half of that;

At the tenth [unit] from the center, three cubits: that is likewise the producing side; \3\

15.s: bāhvorekaviṃśa ubhakaraṇe tathārdho 'nyaśca aṃsaśroṇyośchedastasyobhayato bhavet praugaḥ ||
15.d: बाह्वोरेकविंश उभकरणे तथार्धो ऽन्यश्च अंसश्रोण्योश्छेदस्तस्योभयतो भवेत् प्रौगः ॥
15.m:
On the two arms, twenty-one in both producing sides; and another is half;

The cut of the shoulders and buttocks of it on both sides shall be a prauga. \4\

15.s: cātvālebhyaścaturbhyastu samūhyo 'gniraniṣṭakaḥ digbhyaḥ purīṣaiḥ samūhyo bhāgaśo yuktito vidhiḥ ||
15.d: चात्वालेभ्यश्चतुर्भ्यस्तु समूह्यो ऽग्निरनिष्टकः दिग्भ्यः पुरीषैः समूह्यो भागशो युक्तितो विधिः ॥
15.m:
From the four pits the fire should be piled without bricks;

From the cardinal directions it should be piled with loose earth, part by part, according to the rule and application. \5\

15.s: maṇḍalacaturaśro 'dya parivāryaḥ śmaśānacit droṇacittsarumāneṣāṃ daśabhāgo bhavettsaruḥ ||
15.d: मण्डलचतुरश्रो ऽद्य परिवार्यः श्मशानचित् द्रोणचित्त्सरुमानेषां दशभागो भवेत्त्सरुः ॥
15.m:
Circular and square; now the cemetery-piling is to be enclosed;

For the trough-piling and the hilt-measurement of these, the hilt shall be a tenth part. \6\

15.s: maṇḍale caturaśraṃ tu kuryādgārhapatyavat bāhvorviṃśatibhāgena vāruṇaṃ sārdhameva tu ||
15.d: मण्डले चतुरश्रं तु कुर्याद्गार्हपत्यवत् बाह्वोर्विंशतिभागेन वारुणं सार्धमेव तु ॥
15.m:
