In a circle one should make a square, as in the case of the Gārhapatya [fire],

By a twentieth part of the two arms; but for Varuṇa's [altar], one and a half. \7\

15.s: prasiddhaṃ daśadhā kuryādbahirantaśca yuktitaḥ trikuṣṭhaśca viṣāṇaḥ syātsaṃdhau vyatyāsa eva saḥ ||
15.d: प्रसिद्धं दशधा कुर्याद्बहिरन्तश्च युक्तितः त्रिकुष्ठश्च विषाणः स्यात्संधौ व्यत्यास एव सः ॥
15.m:
One should divide what is established into ten parts, outside and inside, with proper application;

And the horn should be three cubits; at the junction, that indeed is the alternation. \8\

15.s: caturaśrasya karaṇaṃ bāhvordvātriṃśadbhāgikam caturaśramathādhyardhaṃ tābhyāṃ gāyatravadvidhiḥ ||
15.d: चतुरश्रस्य करणं बाह्वोर्द्वात्रिंशद्भागिकम् चतुरश्रमथाध्यर्धं ताभ्यां गायत्रवद्विधिः ॥
15.m:
The producing side of the square is the thirty-second part of the two arms;

A square and then one and a half: by means of those two the rule is as for the Gāyatra [metre]. \9\

15.s: sāhasrasya karaṇaṃ bāhvoḥ pañcadaśabhāgaṃ caturaśram adhyardhāstu tataḥ syurdviśatāścitayaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
15.d: साहस्रस्य करणं बाह्वोः पञ्चदशभागं चतुरश्रम् अध्यर्धास्तु ततः स्युर्द्विशताश्चितयः स्मृताः ॥
15.m:
The producing side for the thousand-[brick altar] is a square of a fifteenth part of the two arms;

Then there should be one-and-a-half [sized bricks]; the brick layers are remembered as two hundred [bricks each]. \10\

15.s: pañca pañcāśatamadhyardhāstisraḥ pañcāśataṃ caturaśrāḥ sahasrācchataṃ pakṣāḥ syuruṣā sahasratamī ||
15.d: पञ्च पञ्चाशतमध्यर्धास्तिस्रः पञ्चाशतं चतुरश्राः सहस्राच्छतं पक्षाः स्युरुषा सहस्रतमी ॥
15.m:
Fifty-five one-and-a-half [bricks], fifty-three square [bricks];

Out of a thousand, a hundred would be wings; the dawn is the thousandth. \11\

15.s: bāhvorekatriṃśo bhāgaḥ karaṇaṃ citistathottarayoḥ caturasrānāṃ sāhasraṃ savanike vyavāsyanti ||
15.d: बाह्वोरेकत्रिंशो भागः करणं चितिस्तथोत्तरयोः चतुरस्रानां साहस्रं सवनिके व्यवास्यन्ति ॥
15.m:
The thirty-first part of the two arms is the producing side; similarly the brick layer of the two upper ones;

A thousand of the squares they assign at the Savanīya [rite]. \12\

15.s: ardhaikādaśapuruṣaṃ ghanaṃ bhavedbhavenmaṇḍalaṃ rathacakram | nābhirarā vivaradhā nemirarebhyo yadyatiriktam ||
15.d: अर्धैकादशपुरुषं घनं भवेद्भवेन्मण्डलं रथचक्रम् । नाभिररा विवरधा नेमिररेभ्यो यद्यतिरिक्तम् ॥
15.m: It should be ten and a half man-lengths solid; the chariot-wheel should be a circle; / The navel, spokes, gaps, and rim—if there is any remainder from the spokes: \13\
Half of that in length of a man-length, extended an eighth part of a man-length; twenty-four having three man-lengths. \14\

15.s: vivarakaraṇamataḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi | dvisaptamena nemyasrakaraṇaṃ bhavedarasyāṣṭabhāgena vaikṛtaścaturviṃśatibhāgena nābhyāmantaramantaro 'ṣṭamabhāgena praugavadbhavet ||
15.d: विवरकरणमतः संप्रवक्ष्यामि । द्विसप्तमेन नेम्यस्रकरणं भवेदरस्याष्टभागेन वैकृतश्चतुर्विंशतिभागेन नाभ्यामन्तरमन्तरो ऽष्टमभागेन प्रौगवद्भवेत् ॥
15.m: Now I shall proclaim the producing side of the gap: / by two-sevenths is the corner-producer of the rim; by an eighth part of a spoke, modified; by a twenty-fourth part, the interval in the navel; the inner by an eighth part becomes like a prauga. \15\

15.s: dvīṣṭakāṃ cinuyānnābhiṃ caturbhiścinuyādarān tribhirnemiṃ yathābhāgaṃ vyatyāsaḥ kūpavat smṛtaḥ ||
15.d: द्वीष्टकां चिनुयान्नाभिं चतुर्भिश्चिनुयादरान् त्रिभिर्नेमिं यथाभागं व्यत्यासः कूपवत् स्मृतः ॥
15.m:
One should pile the navel with two bricks; one should pile the spokes with four;

With three the rim according to share; the alternation is remembered as being like a well. \16\

15.s: viṣkambhasya caturthena nābhyāstu vivaraṃ likhet tricatvāriṃśāṅgulāṃ nemiṃ sārdhacaturaṅgulām ||
15.d: विष्कम्भस्य चतुर्थेन नाभ्यास्तु विवरं लिखेत् त्रिचत्वारिंशाङ्गुलां नेमिं सार्धचतुरङ्गुलाम् ॥
15.m:
By a fourth of the diameter one should draw the opening of the navel;

The rim of forty-three finger-breadths plus four and a half finger-breadths. \17\
The rest is established according to application and whatever correspondences there are in piling. \18\

15.s: ya idamapi yathātathaṃ smṛtiṃ vidhiṃ yadādhītya mimīte rauravaṃ samavati khalu kṛtsnasaṃmato brajati ca śulbakṛtāṃ salokatām ||
15.d: य इदमपि यथातथं स्मृतिं विधिं यदाधीत्य मिमीते रौरवं समवति खलु कृत्स्नसंमतो ब्रजति च शुल्बकृतां सलोकताम् ॥
15.m: Whoever, having studied this tradition and rule just as it is, measures [the altar], protects [himself] completely from Raurava [hell], indeed fully approved by all, and attains the world of the cord-makers. \19\ \\15\\

16.s: rathacakrasya cityasya saṃkṣepoktasya viṣṇunā atha dhāturnirviṣṭhasya triguṇānyaṃ bahirbahiḥ ||
16.d: रथचक्रस्य चित्यस्य संक्षेपोक्तस्य विष्णुना अथ धातुर्निर्विष्ठस्य त्रिगुणान्यं बहिर्बहिः ॥
16.m:
Of the chariot-wheel altar stated in brief by Viṣṇu,

Now, of the fixed element, three times as much [extends] further and further out; \1\

16.s: līyante maṇḍale yasya sapta sārdhā narā budhaiḥ mucyante vivareṣvanye kṣetrādabhyadhikāstrayaḥ ||
16.d: लीयन्ते मण्डले यस्य सप्त सार्धा नरा बुधैः मुच्यन्ते विवरेष्वन्ये क्षेत्रादभ्यधिकास्त्रयः ॥
16.m:
In whose circle seven and a half man-lengths are merged by the wise;

In the gaps the others are left, three in excess of the field. \2\

16.s: tasya cakravidhānaṃ tu nemirarebhyo vistaraḥ maṇḍalānāṃ ca viṣkambhaḥ tribhāgaḥ karaṇāni ca ||
16.d: तस्य चक्रविधानं तु नेमिररेभ्यो विस्तरः मण्डलानां च विष्कम्भः त्रिभागः करणानि च ॥
16.m:
The arrangement of that wheel: the rim is the width from the spokes,

And the diameter of the circles is a third part, and the producing sides; \3\

16.s: narārdhenābhilikhennābhistataḥ prastāragocarā arebhyo 'bhyadhikā nemistriṣaṣṭhenākṣarāgāram triṃśatena saviṃśena adhikaiścārdhapañcamaiḥ mimāyāṅgulairvā madhyaṃ kuryādviṃśena parilekhanam ||
16.d: नरार्धेनाभिलिखेन्नाभिस्ततः प्रस्तारगोचरा अरेभ्यो ऽभ्यधिका नेमिस्त्रिषष्ठेनाक्षरागारम् त्रिंशतेन सविंशेन अधिकैश्चार्धपञ्चमैः मिमायाङ्गुलैर्वा मध्यं कुर्याद्विंशेन परिलेखनम् ॥

16.s: prathame prastare rathacakrasya sṛṇuteṣṭakāḥ caturbhiradhikaṃ vettha catvāriṃśacchatatrayam ||
16.d: प्रथमे प्रस्तरे रथचक्रस्य सृणुतेष्टकाः चतुर्भिरधिकं वेत्थ चत्वारिंशच्छतत्रयम् ॥
16.m:
In the first brick layer of the chariot-wheel [altar], one lays out bricks;

know that there are three hundred and forty-four [bricks]. \5\

16.s: dvitīye 'bhyadhikā yāntu caturviṃśatiriṣṭakāḥ pañcakoṇāstrikoṇāśca nemyarebhyaḥ ca saṃdhiṣu ||
16.d: द्वितीये ऽभ्यधिका यान्तु चतुर्विंशतिरिष्टकाः पञ्चकोणास्त्रिकोणाश्च नेम्यरेभ्यः च संधिषु ॥
16.m:
In the second [layer], let twenty-four bricks be in excess;

five-cornered and three-cornered [bricks are placed] at the joints from the rims and spokes. \6\

16.s: iṣṭakānāṃ sahasreṇa śataiḥ saptabhireva ca aṣṭaṣaṣṭyā ca cakrasya citayaḥ pañca pūritāḥ ||
16.d: इष्टकानां सहस्रेण शतैः सप्तभिरेव च अष्टषष्ट्या च चक्रस्य चितयः पञ्च पूरिताः ॥
16.m:
With one thousand seven hundred

and sixty-eight bricks, the five brick layers of the wheel are completed. \7\
